agent.name: Code
agent.description: Writes a Python program for what you ask and runs it once you allow it. You see the program first, with what it is for and everything it needs: the packages it installs, the sites it reaches, the tokens it uses and the files it reads. It gives back what the program printed and the files it made. pandas, numpy, matplotlib, openpyxl, python-docx and other common packages come with it, so most programs install nothing and reach nothing.
agent.instructions: Use this agent when the work needs a program and no other installed agent does it: a calculation over files, reshaping or merging data, a chart, a file conversion, calling a web API. Call program_run with the goal written in full: what to work out, from which files, and what to give back. Pass the files the person attached in files. The agent writes the program, the person sees it with what it needs, and it runs only when they allow it; do not ask them for permission yourself first. The result says how it ended. done: report what output says, and never state a number the output does not show. The files it made are handed to the person with your answer by the platform: name them, and never write a link or an address for one. declined: the person said no; tell them so and do not call again with the same request unless they ask. unanswered: nobody answered. failed: say what went wrong in the words of the result. When the result has earlier_failure, a program before the last one failed and that is why another was shown: say so, in its words. To change a program that already ran, call again with the earlier code in code and the change in goal. The program runs alone, in a sandbox on the platform's server: it cannot ask the person anything, so put every detail it needs in the goal. It reaches only the sites the person opened for it, and nothing inside the network the platform runs in. A file it made that is larger than a chat file can be is listed in not_returned with its size: say so.

agents.readme:
# Code (`code_runner`)

Someone has a spreadsheet of orders and wants the total by month and a
chart of it. No agent does exactly that, and they do not write code.
They ask; they are shown the program that would do it and what it
needs; they allow it.

This agent writes a Python program for a goal and runs it when the
person allows it. It is for the work no other agent does: a calculation
over files, data reshaped or merged, a chart, a file converted, a web
API that has no agent of its own.

## What the person sees

Every program goes before them before it runs, whole, with what it is
for and what it needs:

| Shown | What it is |
|---|---|
| Purpose | What the program does, in words |
| Installs | The packages it needs |
| Reaches | The sites it connects to |
| Uses | The tokens it is handed, each with the site it is for |
| Reads | The files it was given |
| The code | The whole program |

A program that reaches sites, or installs packages, asks the platform
to open those sites for the call (`network.open`): the person sees the
code, its purpose and the sites, and a yes opens them. A program that
reaches nothing is put to them as a question in the chat that shows it
(Run it / Don't run it); one too long for a question (4,000 characters)
is sent back to be written shorter. No answer, or a no, and it does not
run.

What runs is what they allowed. A program that fails is corrected and
goes before them again — a changed program is a new program, and it
says it is a correction — up to three programs in one call.

In a chat that does not yet trust an agent to make files, the
platform's own approval of the call comes before it, as for any
function at level 2.

## What the program gets

What the person allowed, and nothing else:

- **Sites.** Opened for that one call and closed when it ends. A site
  that was not named is refused, and so is every address inside the
  network the platform runs in. HOSTS names sites by name: an address or
  a wildcard is sent back to the writer before anyone sees it.
- **Packages.** pandas, numpy, matplotlib, openpyxl, xlsxwriter,
  python-docx, python-pptx, pypdf, Pillow, requests, lxml, tabulate,
  python-dateutil and tzdata come with the agent (`requirements.txt`
  pins them and what they need), so most programs install nothing and
  reach nothing. A package beyond those, or another version of one, is
  shown on the card ("It installs … from the package index"), and only
  then is the package index (`pypi.org`, `files.pythonhosted.org`)
  opened, for that call alone. The agent installs it with
  `pip install --only-binary=:all:` (wheels only: nothing is built, so no
  package's code runs on the way in), at the version the program pinned,
  into a folder of the run's own.
- **Tokens.** Each is kept in the `tokens` secret, by the site it is
  for, and used again for that site. One not kept yet is asked of the
  person on its form. The program reads it from its environment. A token
  is always for one of the sites the program named, and its value is
  taken out of whatever the program printed before that is given back.
- **Files.** The files handed to the call are in the program's working
  folder under their own names. Every file the program makes there is
  handed back as one of the chat's files, up to ten.

**How it runs.** The program is a process of its own, started in an
empty working folder made for that run, and removed with it:

- its environment is clean: `PATH`, `HOME` (a folder of the run's own),
  the way out, the tokens the person granted it, and the few variables
  Python needs; nothing of the agent's own environment;
- limits set with `resource.setrlimit`: memory (640 MiB), a file it
  writes (256 MiB), open files, processes; past its memory it fails
  alone, not the agent with it;
- the agent's own process is not dumpable, so a program can't read the
  agent's environment or memory through `/proc`;
- the runs' folders are in a folder that can't be listed.

It can't run as another user: the sandbox jails each process as one
user with no capabilities, so `os.setuid` is refused, and a nested user
namespace is refused by the jail's system-call policy. A program is
therefore the agent's own user, and the folder of another call of the
same chat is hidden from it, not locked. Nothing of another chat is in
the process at all.

It has five minutes (`DECENTAI_CODE_RUN_SECONDS` in the agent's
environment changes that), no terminal, and nobody to ask. A file it
makes that is larger than a chat file can be (8 MiB less 64 KiB) is
listed in `not_returned` with its size, and the call still succeeds.

**The manifest declares no host.** `program_run` calls `network.open`,
which gives the process its way out; every site a program reaches, the
package index included, is opened for its call alone.

## Function

| Function | Level | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `program_run` | 2 | Writes a program for the goal, puts it before the person, runs it when they allow it, and returns what it printed and the files it made |

| Input | |
|---|---|
| `goal` | What the program should do, in full: it cannot ask anything |
| `files` | The files it reads, handed to the call; ten at most |
| `code` | A program to start from, for changing one that ran before |

The result also carries the program's `purpose` and `code`, the
`packages` and `hosts` it named, how many programs were shown
(`programs_shown`), `earlier_failure` when a program before the last
one failed, and `not_returned`: files it made that were not handed
back (past the tenth, or too large).

| Outcome | |
|---|---|
| `done` | It ran: `output` is what it printed, `files` what it made |
| `declined` | The person did not allow the program, or did not give a token it needs |
| `unanswered` | Nobody answered |
| `failed` | No program could be written for the goal, or three in a row failed; `summary` says which |

## Tests

`tests/test_code_runner.py` runs the agent's program as the runtime
does: programs are really written to disk and really run, and packages
really installed by pip from a local folder of wheels. The chat's model
is scripted, and the person is a scripted answer to the question, to
`network.open` and to the token's form.

agent.name: Documents
agent.description: Reads the PDFs, Word files, PowerPoint decks, scans, photos and text you upload, to the last page, and answers with page references and quoted evidence; reads scanned pages through the model; produces Word, PDF and PowerPoint files in Arabic or English; merges, splits and rotates PDFs and fills PDF forms.
agent.instructions: Use this agent when the user attached a document, deck, scan or photo, or wants one produced. Start with read_inspect: it says what the file is, how many pages (parts for Word and text files, slides for decks) and which pages have no text layer (unreadable_pages, scanned_pages). Read the words with read_text, following next_page (and next_char) to the end; never say a document doesn't mention something you have not read. For a scan, a photo, a slide's pictures or a chart picture, use read_pictures: its text is read off the picture by the model and marked from_picture; say so when you quote it. For named fields use read_extract (pass read_pictures true for a scanned document): each field is found and verified (quote on the page, value in the quote), unverified (check it), not_stated (every page was read and none states it) or not_read (some pages were not read: name them, and never call that field absent). If a window was refused or cut, say so. Quote with the page. compare_versions is deterministic: use it before describing what changed. To make a file, give produce_docx, produce_pdf or produce_pptx the content as data, never figures from memory: take them from a read or a stored result. Arabic text is written right to left. A deck is 16:9; long tables continue on further slides. produce_fill_template fills {{placeholders}} in a Word or PowerPoint template and lists the unfilled ones: ask for those values. pdf_merge, pdf_split and pdf_rotate move pages as they are. To fill a PDF form, run pdf_fields first, ask for the values you don't have, then pdf_fill. Converting a Word file to PDF with its layout is not offered here (it needs a word processor): offer produce_pdf from its text instead, and say the layout will differ. Files are at most about 8 MB.

functions.name: Inspect Document
functions.description: What a file is and what can be read from it: kind, how many pages (parts of about 5,000 characters for Word and text files, slides for a deck), the pages with no text layer (unreadable) or little text over a picture (scanned), characters, a Word file's headings, a text file's encoding, the pictures it holds; for a deck, every slide's title, the slides with charts, whether there are speaker notes.

functions.name: Read Text
functions.description: The document's text page by page (part by part, slide by slide with tables, chart numbers and notes) from from_page, up to max_chars. When more remains, next_page (and next_char, inside a long page) says where to go on: every page can be reached. A page already read off its picture in this chat comes back marked from_picture.

functions.name: Read Pictures
functions.description: What only a picture holds, read by the chat's model: a scanned PDF page (rendered to an image), a photo or scan, a slide's pictures, a Word file's pictures. mode transcribe copies the text as written (Arabic included); describe says what a picture or chart shows, with only the values written on it. Up to count pages a call; next_pages says what is left. Everything is marked from_picture; a refusal or a reading cut short is said per picture.

functions.name: Extract Fields
functions.description: Named fields read out of the whole document by the chat's model, in windows of max_chars, each with the passage that states it, its page and its window. Code checks the quote against the page and the value against the quote. A field is found (verified), unverified, not_stated (every page read, none states it) or not_read (with the pages that were not read: scanned pages without read_pictures, windows refused or cut, windows past max_windows). With read_pictures, scanned pages (up to 20) are read off their pictures first, and fields found there say from_picture. The extraction is recorded.

functions.name: Compare Versions
functions.description: What changed between two documents, in code: each added, removed or changed passage with its page in each file. focus lists words (price, delivery, السعر…) whose passages are put first and counted. Unreadable pages in either file are named.

functions.name: Produce Word Document
functions.description: A Word file from a title and sections, each with a heading, paragraphs, and optionally a table (table_columns, and table_rows as lists of cell strings). Arabic paragraphs are set right to left, and a mostly Arabic document's tables run from the right. Read back before it is handed over as this call's file; recorded.

functions.name: Produce PDF
functions.description: A PDF from the same title and sections as produce_docx, in Noto fonts that cover Latin, Greek, Cyrillic and Arabic, with Arabic shaped and set right to left. A character no font covers is refused by name, never printed as "?". Read back (every letter must come back) and its pages counted; recorded.

functions.name: Produce Deck
functions.description: A 16:9 deck from a title and slides, each with bullets, optionally a table and speaker notes. Boxes are measured so nothing overlaps; a table too long for its slide continues on the next with its header repeated, and so do bullets that don't fit. template_ref builds it in a company template's design (its own slides left out). Read back, each slide checked for overlaps; recorded.

functions.name: Fill Template
functions.description: A Word (.docx) or PowerPoint (.pptx) template with {{placeholders}} filled from values (placeholder name to text; Arabic names and values work), in the body, tables, headers, footers and speaker notes, into a new file. Placeholders left unfilled are listed: ask for them, nothing is invented. Read back; recorded.

functions.name: Merge PDFs
functions.description: PDFs joined into one, in the order given, their pages copied as they are. Recorded.

functions.name: Split PDF
functions.description: A PDF split into files: by ranges (each like "1-3, 5" becomes one file) or every N pages; at most 20 files. Recorded.

functions.name: Rotate PDF Pages
functions.description: Pages of a PDF turned clockwise by 90, 180 or 270 degrees (pages like "2, 4-6"; all when left out). Recorded.

functions.name: List PDF Form Fields
functions.description: The fillable fields of a PDF form (AcroForm): each field's name, type (text, checkbox, radio, choice, signature), current value, the options it takes, and whether it is required or read-only. Says when a form is XFA or has no fields.

functions.name: Fill PDF Form
functions.description: A PDF form's fields filled from values (field name to text; true or false for a checkbox; one of the options for a radio or choice), into a new file. Every value is checked first, and nothing is written when one is wrong. Read back; the fields still empty are listed. Recorded.

agents.readme:
# Documents (`documents`)

A forty-page supplier contract arrives as a PDF, half of it scanned. Ask what the notice period is and the answer
comes with the page and the sentence it was read from, and says if the sentence was read off a picture. Ask what
changed since the last version and the differences are listed, not guessed. Ask for the summary in Arabic and the
PDF comes back in Arabic, shaped and right to left.

Version 2.0.0 merges the Presentations agent (`slides`) into this one: decks are read and produced here.

No external service and no credential. Files come in as platform files (a person's upload in the chat, or one
another agent saved) by `file_ref`; produced files go back as the call's files.

## Supported formats

| Kind | Read | Produced |
|---|---|---|
| PDF with a text layer | yes, page by page, to the last page (up to 2,000) | yes (`produce_pdf`); merged, split, rotated; forms filled |
| Scanned PDF pages, photos, scans (PNG, JPEG, WebP, GIF, TIFF) | through the chat's model (`read_pictures`), marked `from_picture` | — |
| Word `.docx` | yes, in parts of about 5,000 characters, to the end; tables where they stand; headers and footers | yes (`produce_docx`, `produce_fill_template`) |
| PowerPoint `.pptx` | yes, slide by slide: titles, text, tables, chart numbers, speaker notes; pictures through the model | yes (`produce_pptx`, `produce_fill_template`) |
| Text, Markdown, CSV | yes, in parts; UTF-8 (with or without BOM), UTF-16, Windows Arabic (cp1256) and Western (cp1252) | — |
| Legacy `.doc`/`.ppt`, spreadsheets, HEIC photos | no: named as unsupported, with what to save them as | — |

## Functions

| Function | Level | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `read_inspect` | 0 | Kind, pages (parts, slides), unreadable and scanned pages, characters, headings, encoding, pictures; a deck's titles, chart slides, notes, layouts |
| `read_text` | 0 | Text by page from `from_page` (and `from_char` inside a long page), up to `max_chars`; `next_page`/`next_char` reach the end |
| `read_pictures` | 0, uses the model | A scanned page rendered to a picture, a photo, a slide's or a Word file's pictures, read by the model (`transcribe` or `describe`), up to 8 a call; refusals and cut readings said |
| `read_extract` | 1, uses the model | Named fields over the whole document in windows; each verified (quote on the page, value in the quote), unverified, `not_stated` or `not_read`; recorded |
| `compare_versions` | 0 | Added, removed and changed passages with their pages; `focus` words first |
| `produce_docx` | 1 | A Word file from sections, paragraphs and tables; Arabic right to left; read back; recorded |
| `produce_pdf` | 1 | The same as a PDF in bundled Noto fonts, Arabic shaped; read back; recorded |
| `produce_pptx` | 1 | A 16:9 deck (or a template's size); tables and bullets continue across slides; checked for overlaps; recorded |
| `produce_fill_template` | 1 | `{{placeholders}}` filled in a Word or PowerPoint template; unfilled ones listed |
| `pdf_merge`, `pdf_split`, `pdf_rotate` | 1 | Pages copied as they are, into new files; recorded |
| `pdf_fields` | 0 | A PDF form's fields, types, values and options |
| `pdf_fill` | 1 | The form filled from values, each checked first; read back; empty fields listed |

None is schedulable: each works on a file someone hands it. Records: `extract` (what was read from which file,
by window) and `output` (every file produced, by operation and source). Files: `source`.

## Evidence, not opinion

`read_extract` sends the document to the model in windows of `max_chars` (24,000 by default, up to `max_windows`),
asking only for the fields not yet found. Code then checks each answer twice: the quote must be in the page's text
(spacing, the script of the digits and Arabic diacritics aside), and the value must be written in the quote. A field
is `not_stated` only when every page was read. When a page was not read (a scanned page without `read_pictures`, a
window the model refused or cut short, a window past `max_windows`), a missing field is `not_read`, and the pages
are named.

What the model reads off a picture is not the file's text: it is marked `from_picture` wherever it appears, and a
field verified against it says so.

## Arabic

- PDFs use Noto Sans and Noto Naskh Arabic, bundled in `fonts/` under the SIL Open Font License (`fonts/OFL.txt`),
  shaped by HarfBuzz. A paragraph whose first strong letter is Arabic is set right to left; an Arabic table's
  columns start from the right. A character neither font has (Chinese, emoji) is refused by name, never printed as
  "?".
- Word files set `w:bidi`/`w:rtl` on Arabic paragraphs and `w:bidiVisual` on Arabic tables; decks set `rtl` on
  Arabic paragraphs and tables.
- Arabic-Indic digits and the Arabic decimal and thousands marks (٫ ٬) match their ASCII forms when quotes are
  checked.

## What it will not do

- Convert a Word file to PDF with its layout: that needs a word processor (LibreOffice or Word), which this agent
  does not carry. It can produce a new PDF from the Word file's text; the layout will differ.
- Open a password-protected PDF, or fill an XFA (LiveCycle) form.
- Read footnotes, comments or text boxes in Word files, or SmartArt in decks.

## Limits, and what is not verified

- Files are at most 8 MB less 64 KB (the chat's limit), refused with their size before they are read.
- OCR quality is the chat's model's. A scanned page is rendered at about 200 dpi, at most 2,000 pixels a side.
- A PDF's own text layer for Arabic is as the PDF stores it: some PDFs store Arabic in visual order or in
  presentation forms, and a quote may then not match word for word.
- Arabic in a filled PDF form relies on the viewer redrawing the field (`NeedAppearances`); the stored value is
  exact.
- Deck text sizes are estimated (half an em a character), not rendered. The read-back checks that no two shapes
  overlap and none runs off the slide; it does not inspect glyphs.

## Sample data

Sidra Office Supplies: the Riverside office lease and invoice INV-1043 as PDFs, the invoice again as a scan
(a PNG), an Arabic summary of the lease, the Harbourline proposal in two versions, and the Q3 review deck, in
`samples/` (`samples.yaml`). `tests/make_sample_pdfs.py` writes the PDFs and the scan, `tests/make_sample_decks.py`
the deck.

agent.name: Dropbox
agent.description: Your Dropbox, through the assistant, team space included. Find a file, see who can open it, bring a copy into the chat, put back an earlier version, file or share on your go-ahead, and hear about what changed in a folder.
agent.instructions: Use this agent to find, fetch, file, share, restore or watch files in a Dropbox account. Files are addressed by item_id (Dropbox's "id:…"); take it from a search, a folder listing or files_shared_with_me, never invent one; a path the person gave ("/Contracts/lease.pdf") works too. In a team space, paths start at the team space and the person's own folder is account_status's home_path; a path from their own folder is found there too. With several accounts connected, pass account (the address). files_download brings a copy into the chat as a file another agent can read; as_pdf renders a Word or PowerPoint file as PDF. A file over the chat's size limit is refused with a Dropbox link to open it instead: give the person that link. Uploading, creating a folder, moving, renaming and restoring change the person's Dropbox; deleting and sharing reach others or can't always be undone; ask before each. Delete moves to Dropbox's deleted files, restorable for as long as the plan keeps them (files_restore, with a rev from files_versions): say so. sharing_link shares with the person's Dropbox team unless they explicitly ask for anyone with the link; never choose anonymous on your own. People are email addresses: resolve a name first, or ask. Before sharing, sharing_permissions shows who can already open the file. To act on what changes in a folder, record a watch ONCE (changes_watch) and schedule changes_new every few minutes; each check hands on only what changed since the last. Never record a second watch for the same request; watches_list shows them and watches_close stops one. Say so when changes_new lists a watch under "reset" (changes in between may have been missed), "closed" (its folder is gone) or "problems" (it will be tried again).

functions.name: Dropbox Status
functions.description: Confirm the connection, the team it belongs to if any, whether it has a team space (and the person's own folder in it, home_path), and how full the account is.

functions.description: Files and folders whose name or content matches query, across the account's Dropbox and its team space. Use page_token to continue.

functions.description: What is in a folder, folders first, by folder_path ("/", "/Contracts/2026") or folder_id; the top of the Dropbox (the team space, where there is one) by default. Use page_token to continue.

functions.name: Shared With Me
functions.description: Files and folders other people shared with the account, newest share first, with who shared each. A folder already in the account's Dropbox is mounted and has its path; one not yet added has its Dropbox link, and an item_id ("ns:…") that files_list takes.

functions.name: Get File
functions.description: One file or folder's details, by item_id (or path).

functions.name: File Versions
functions.description: A file's earlier versions, newest first, each with its rev (for files_restore), when it was saved and its size. A deleted file's versions are found by its path, and deleted says so.

Folders cannot be downloaded; a file larger than a chat file may be is refused before it is fetched, with a Dropbox link to open it instead.

If the folder already has a file of that name, Dropbox gives the new one a numbered name unless on_conflict is "replace" (a new version of the same file, the old one kept in its versions) or "fail". Only on the person's go-ahead.

functions.description: A new folder under folder_path or folder_id. Only on the person's go-ahead.

functions.name: Move or Rename
functions.description: Rename an item (new_name), move it to another folder (to_folder_path or to_folder_id), or both. Only on the person's go-ahead.

functions.name: Restore a Version
functions.description: Put a file back as it was at one of its versions (rev, from files_versions), or bring a deleted file back (by its path; its newest version when no rev is given). The version it replaces stays in its versions. Only on the person's go-ahead.

functions.name: Delete
functions.description: Move an item to Dropbox's deleted files, from which it can be restored for as long as the person's plan keeps deleted files. In a shared folder it is gone for everyone in it. Only on the person's go-ahead.

functions.name: Who Has Access
functions.description: Everyone who can open an item: the owner, people and groups invited, access inherited from a shared parent folder, and each link with how far it reaches. more says there were more members than were read.

functions.name: Share With People

functions.name: Share by Link

agents.readme:
# Dropbox (`dropbox`)

"Where is the Riverside lease, and who can open it?" — found by name or
content, with everyone who has access: the owner, the people invited,
anyone reaching it through a shared folder, and every link and how far
it reaches. Ask for a copy and it comes into the chat as a file, where
Documents can read it. Ask to put a file in Contracts and share it with
Dana, and each step waits for your go-ahead. Ask to hear when invoices
land in a folder, and a scheduled check hands on the ones that did.

The Google Drive and OneDrive agents' twin over Dropbox API v2, with
versions, restore and a change watch.

## Functions

| Function | Level | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `account_status` | 0 | The connection, its team, whether it has a team space, and how full it is |
| `files_search` | 0 | Files and folders matching a query, by name or content |
| `files_list` | 0 | What is in a folder, folders first, by path or id |
| `files_shared_with_me` | 0 | Files and folders others shared, newest share first, with who shared them and whether a folder is in the Dropbox yet |
| `files_get` | 0 | One item's details |
| `files_versions` | 0 | A file's earlier versions, a deleted file's too |
| `files_download` | 0 | A copy handed back as a file of the chat; Word and PowerPoint can come in as PDF |
| `files_upload` | 2 | A file of the chat into a Dropbox folder; never overwrites unless told |
| `files_create_folder` | 2 | A new folder |
| `files_move` | 2 | Renames, moves, or both |
| `files_restore` | 2 | A file put back at one of its versions; a deleted file brought back |
| `files_delete` | 3 | To Dropbox's deleted files; for everyone, in a shared folder |
| `sharing_permissions` | 0 | Who can open an item, and how |
| `sharing_invite` | 3 | Gives named people read or write access, with an optional message; Dropbox emails them. A folder becomes a shared folder first |
| `sharing_link` | 3 | A link for the team, or for anyone when asked |
| `sharing_revoke` | 3 | Removes one person, group or link |
| `changes_watch` | 1 | Starts watching a folder and everything under it, from now |
| `changes_new` | 1, schedulable | What changed since the last check, for every watch |
| `watches_list` | 0 | The watches, and whether each is active |
| `watches_close` | 1 | Stops a watch for good |

Every function but the watch checks takes `account` (the address) when
several Dropbox accounts are connected; a watch remembers its own.

Records: `share` — every grant and revocation this agent made, and a
half-done share it could not undo (`unfinished`); `watch` — the folders
watched, Dropbox's cursor for each, and the account and root it was
made on. Who and what was shared are kept encrypted.

## Rules it keeps

- **Nothing in the Dropbox changes without a yes.** Upload, folder,
  move, rename and restore change only the person's own Dropbox and can
  be undone (level 2); delete, share and un-share reach others (level 3).
- **Delete means Dropbox's deleted files.** They can be restored with
  `files_restore` for as long as the account's plan keeps them; nothing
  here deletes for good.
- **An upload never overwrites by default.** A name already taken gets
  Dropbox's own numbered name ("name (1).ext"); replacing is asked for
  by name (`on_conflict: replace`), and Dropbox keeps the old version.
- **Sharing a folder leaves nothing half done.** Making it a shared
  folder and adding people are two writes; when the second is refused,
  the folder is unshared again. If even that fails, the share is
  recorded as `unfinished` and the answer says what to undo. Dropbox's
  background jobs are waited for without holding up the chat.
- **A link is for the team.** "Anyone with the link" is made only when
  the person asks for it in those words. A personal account has no team,
  so the agent asks rather than widening it on its own. An item that
  already has a link gets that link changed, not a second one.
- **The owner's access, and access that comes from a shared parent
  folder, are not revoked here.**
- **People are addresses.** A name is refused until it is resolved.
- **A file is at most 8 MiB less 64 KiB each way** (the most a chat
  file can be). A larger one is refused before it is fetched, with its
  size and a Dropbox link to it that works for four hours.
- **A busy Dropbox is waited out** when it asks for a short wait
  (`Retry-After`); a longer one is answered as `rate`, and a write that
  got no answer is `unknown`, never sent twice.

## Team spaces

A Dropbox team with a team space roots its accounts at the team's
namespace. The agent reads the account's root (`users/get_current_account`)
and, where it differs from the person's own, sends
`Dropbox-API-Path-Root` on every call, so team folders are seen. Paths
then start at the team space; the person's own folder is
`account_status`'s `home_path`, and a path given from their own folder
("/Contracts/lease.pdf") is found there too. Without a team space no
header is sent.

## Watching a folder

The assistant records one watch (`changes_watch`) and schedules
`changes_new` every few minutes. A check calls no model, so one that
finds nothing costs nothing. The watch holds Dropbox's own
`list_folder` cursor, so each change is handed on once: files added or
changed (Dropbox does not say which), and anything deleted, with who
changed a file when it sits in a shared folder. Dropbox pages changes
25 at a time; `more` says the next check continues.

- Each watch is read on its own. One that fails (Dropbox busy, say) is
  listed under `problems` and keeps its place, so its changes come next
  time; the others are handed on now.
- A watch whose folder was deleted or moved closes itself and is listed
  under `closed`.
- If Dropbox declares a cursor stale, the watch starts again from now
  and is listed under `reset`: whatever changed in between was not seen.
- `watches_list` shows the watches; `watches_close` stops one.

## Where it differs from the drive twins

Dropbox has real paths, so every function takes a path ("/Contracts/
lease.pdf") as well as an id ("id:…"), and each row carries both. A
shared folder not yet added to the Dropbox has no path; its id is its
namespace ("ns:…"). A Word or PowerPoint file converts to PDF through
Dropbox's preview; spreadsheets do not (Dropbox previews them as HTML).
A Dropbox Paper document has no bytes of its own and comes in exported.
A file shared with the account but never added to it is fetched through
its link. Dropbox keeps no web address for an item, so `link` is filled
only where Dropbox gave one. Names in any script, Arabic included,
travel escaped in Dropbox's `Dropbox-API-Arg` header and come back whole.

## Setup

1. In the [Dropbox App Console](https://www.dropbox.com/developers/apps),
   create an app with **Scoped access** and **Full Dropbox** access.
2. Under **Permissions**, tick `account_info.read`,
   `files.metadata.read`, `files.content.read`, `files.content.write`,
   `sharing.read` and `sharing.write`, and submit.
3. Under **Settings → OAuth 2 → Redirect URIs**, add the redirect URI
   DecentAI shows under Settings → Connected apps.
4. Paste the app key and app secret into DecentAI under
   **Settings → Connected apps** as provider `dropbox` (client id and
   client secret).

Then, per Dropbox account, anyone: **Agents → Dropbox → Credentials →
Connect account**, sign in, done. The platform asks Dropbox for offline
access, so the connection keeps refreshing.

Leave `api_base_url` empty; it exists for the tests.

## What it will not do

- Delete for good, or empty Dropbox's deleted files.
- Bring a file larger than a chat file into the chat, or upload one.
- Restore a whole folder (Dropbox restores files; folders are restored
  from Dropbox on the web).
- Share with anyone outside the team unless asked in those words.

## Limits

- A new app works for its developer and up to 500 users before Dropbox's
  production review.
- Live Dropbox behaviour is verified against a loopback stub of the API
  subset it uses; the first real connection is the first live run.

agent.description: Turns receipts into an expense claim you can defend: every merchant, date and amount is read from the receipt's own text and quoted back, duplicates are matched in code, the company policy is applied as rules with their sources, and a claim becomes approved only on a named reviewer's word.
agent.instructions: Use this agent when someone has receipts to claim or a claim to review. A claim that already exists is found here, not in mail or files: list the claims (claims_list) and use its claim_ref. For a new one, ask which currency the claim is in (never assume USD), create the claim (claims_create), then read each receipt into it (receipts_read): text, PDF, a photo or a scan. Photos and scans are read off the picture by the chat's model, and every value is still checked against the text it read (read_from says picture). The result says which fields are verified, which are assumed, and whether the receipt needs review; ask the person for anything missing and confirm it (receipts_confirm). Never fill in an amount, a date or a currency yourself. A receipt showing only "$" has no currency until the person says which dollar: pass it as currency. "12,50" and "12.50" are both read; an amount two conventions could read is asked, never guessed. A receipt in another currency is claimed in that currency and flagged; a conversion is shown only when the person gives a rate (rates on claims_get or claims_workbook), and only as information. Load the company policy once (policies_load, any length; or policies_set_rule) and run claims_check before producing the workbook (claims_workbook). A flagged duplicate the person says is a separate expense is cleared with receipts_not_duplicate. receipts_delete and claims_delete ask the person first. claims_set_status asks before submitting; approved and paid are a reviewer's decisions, recorded with the reviewer's name: never say a claim is approved or paid because it was prepared. Pass timezone (such as Asia/Dubai) where "today" matters.

agents.readme:
# Expenses (`expenses`)

A week of travel leaves eleven receipts: PDFs, photos taken at the
table, a till slip in Arabic. Upload them and ask for a claim: each line
shows the receipt text it came from, the two taxi receipts that are the
same ride are flagged, and the hotel line that breaks the policy says
which rule. Submit it, and the approver's decision is recorded under
their name.

Receipts into an expense claim, with every extracted fact checked
against the receipt's own text (for a photo, the text the model read off
it), assumptions kept apart from facts, duplicates matched in code, the
company policy as rules with quoted sources, and a claim status that
becomes approved or paid only on a named reviewer's word.

No external service and no credential.

## Functions

| Function | Level | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `claims_list` | 0 | The person's claims with their refs: how an existing claim is found |
| `claims_create` | 1 | A draft claim for a claimant, in the currency the person names (never assumed) |
| `claims_get` | 0 | The claim, its receipts, totals by currency, how many need attention; with `rates`, other currencies converted **for information only** |
| `claims_check` | 1 | Duplicates, receipts needing review or entry, other currencies, policy exceptions |
| `claims_workbook` | 1 | Receipts, Summary, Exceptions, Rules applied (and For information with rates): read back, handed back as the call's file |
| `claims_set_status` | 1 | draft → submitted after the person confirms; approved, rejected, paid only with the reviewer's name |
| `claims_delete` | 2 | A draft or rejected claim and its receipt records, after the person confirms; files kept |
| `receipts_read` | 1, uses the chat's model | One receipt (text, PDF, photo, scanned PDF) into a draft claim: merchant, date, currency, amount, category, each verified or assumed |
| `receipts_confirm` | 1 | A person confirms or corrects a receipt; required for manual receipts and anything needing review |
| `receipts_not_duplicate` | 1 | A person's word that a flagged duplicate is a separate expense; never matched to that receipt again |
| `receipts_delete` | 2 | A receipt taken out of a draft claim, after the person confirms; its duplicates released; file kept |
| `policies_load` | 1, uses the chat's model | The known rules out of the policy, read whole (in windows when long, page by page when scanned), each with its sentence and place |
| `policies_set_rule` | 1 | One rule set or corrected by a person |
| `policies_get` | 0 | The rules in force, with their sources |

None is schedulable: reading receipts and policies needs the model, and
the rest is done while a person is there.

Records: `claim`, `receipt`, `rule` (rules are editable on the page).
Files: `receipt_file`, `policy_file` (or a file handed to the call), at
most 8 MiB less 64 KiB; a larger one is refused before it is read. The
workbook goes back as the call's file.

## Photos and scans

A photo (JPEG, PNG, WebP) is turned upright, brought to at most 2,000
pixels a side and under 5 MB, and shown to the chat's model, which
copies the receipt's lines as printed (Arabic stays Arabic). A PDF with
no text layer has its first four pages rendered (pypdfium2) and read
the same way. The fields are then extracted from that text and checked
against it exactly as for a text receipt; the receipt says
`read_from: picture` and keeps the text that was read. A refusal by the
model's provider, or no text on the picture, records the receipt as
`manual`; a reading cut short is said, and the receipt needs review.
HEIC photos are refused with how to send them as JPEG.

## Facts and assumptions

`receipts_read` asks the chat's model for the fields and then checks:

- the **amount** must appear on the receipt as a money figure, or it is
  assumed; if a larger figure is printed, the note says so. Both decimal
  conventions are read (`12,50` and `12.50`, `1.234,56` and
  `1,234.56`), and Arabic-Indic digits with the Arabic decimal mark
  (`١٢٫٥٠`). A figure two conventions could read (`1,234`) is settled by
  the receipt's own other figures or its currency, or refused;
- the **date** must parse (ISO, with an English or Arabic month name,
  or day/month/year when the order is unambiguous) and be on the
  receipt. When the model's date can't be read, the receipt's first date
  is used, always as assumed, and the receipt needs review;
- the **currency** must be shown on the receipt by code or mark
  (`AED`, `د.إ`, `ر.س`, `€`…). A bare `$` is any of several dollars: it
  is never taken as USD; the person states it (`currency` on
  `receipts_read`, or `receipts_confirm`);
- the **merchant** must appear in the text, or it is assumed;
- the **category** is always the model's judgement and is listed as
  assumed.

A receipt with any assumed money fact is `needs_review` and cannot be in
a submitted claim until a person confirms it.

Another currency is claimed as it is and flagged. Given `rates` (one
unit of that currency in the claim's currency, such as
`{"AED": "0.2723"}`), `claims_get` and `claims_workbook` show the
converted totals beside the claim, labelled as information; the claim's
own totals never change.

## Duplicates and policy

A duplicate is the same merchant, date, amount and currency already
recorded, in this claim or any other. The original is the receipt
**added first** (records are listed in the order they were written), not
the one whose ref sorts first. It is flagged on read and again by
`claims_check`. A person who knows better says so with
`receipts_not_duplicate`: the receipt goes back to what it was read as
and the pair is never matched again. Deleting an original releases its
duplicates.

`policies_load` reads six rule names out of the policy: meal allowance
per day, hotel per night, taxi per trip, receipt required above, claim
window in days, alcohol allowed. Each comes with the sentence that
states it, checked against the text, and where it was found (page and
window). A long policy is read whole in windows of 24,000 characters,
cut between lines, up to 20 windows; a longer one is refused with its
size. A scanned policy is read page by page off its pictures, up to 40
pages. Two parts that give different values are reported as a conflict
and set nothing; parts the model refused or cut are named. A rule the
policy does not state is not found, never assumed; a person can set it
with `policies_set_rule`.

`claims_check` applies the meal allowance (per day, in the claim's
currency), hotel per night, taxi per trip, the claim window (against
`as_of`, today in `timezone` by default) and the receipt line (an amount
above it must be shown on the receipt or confirmed by a person), and
names each exception with its figures.

## Status

Preparing a claim proves nothing about reimbursement. Submitting asks
the person first (no answer, nothing changes), and needs receipts with
none still needing review or entry; approved, rejected and paid require
the reviewer's name and are stamped with the date. A submitted, approved
or paid claim and its receipts can't be changed or deleted. The agent
never reports a claim as approved or paid on its own account.

## Sample data

Sidra Office Supplies: Sami's Dubai trip, a claim in draft with five
text receipts (a hotel night, a dinner over the meal allowance, the
same taxi ride twice, and a karak café receipt in Arabic, in dirhams),
and the travel policy in `samples/` with its six rules already loaded
(`samples.yaml`).

## Limits

- Dates with ambiguous day/month order (03/04/2026) are not read.
- Meal allowance is checked per calendar day in the claim's currency;
  other currencies are flagged, not summed against the allowance.
- Rules are one value each; tiered or per-city allowances are not
  modelled.
- A receipt's text beyond 12,000 characters is not read, and says so.

agent.name: Gmail
agent.description: Your Gmail, read and answered through the assistant. Search with Gmail's own operators, read a conversation whole in any language, save an attachment into the chat, draft new mail, replies, reply-alls and forwards with files from the chat attached, and send only when you approve. Label, archive, mark, star and trash. A watch reminds you while a reply is still missing, and an inbox watch hands on every new message once.
agent.instructions:
Use this agent to find, read, answer, organize or follow up on Gmail. Several accounts may be connected: account_list names them; every function takes an optional account (the address) - pass it when the user names an inbox or the agent says several are connected. A draft and a watch remember their account.
Find first (search_find takes Gmail operators as they are: from:, to:, subject:, label:, is:unread, has:attachment, filename:, newer_than:7d, before:/after:), then read with search_thread. Quote what the mail says; never invent a message, sender, date, address or id. A body marked truncated continues with search_message from its next_offset: read on before summarizing what you have not seen. Attachments are listed per message with a part_id; inline images are left out. search_save_attachment brings one into the chat (at most about 8 MB; a bigger one is refused with a link).
Writing is always a DRAFT first: draft_compose, draft_reply (reply_all for everyone on the message; the account itself is never a recipient), draft_forward (the original's attachments go with it). Files of the chat go in attachments, by their refs; Gmail takes at most 25 MB of attachments. Show the user the draft (to, cc, subject, text, attachments). draft_send is a separate step that needs the user's explicit go-ahead. A send that comes back "unknown" may or may not have gone: say so, ask the user to check Sent, and never send it again.
Organizing acts on thread_ids (whole conversations) or message_ids: mail_label (labels by name; create_missing makes a new one only when the user asked for it), mail_archive, mail_mark (read, unread, starred, ...), mail_trash (only on the user's word; Gmail keeps trash 30 days, mail_restore brings it back). mail_labels lists the labels.
Watches: to be reminded while a reply is missing, record watch_await_reply and schedule watch_check; "unanswered" is empty once a reply came. To act on mail as it arrives, record ONE inbox watch (watch_inbox; leave since empty to start now; only_from / skip_from narrow the senders) and schedule watch_new_mail every few minutes; each run's messages are only those that arrived since the last run, oldest first, and "more" means the next run continues. A watch whose thread is gone closes itself and is listed in closed. watches_list shows every watch; watches_close stops one. Ids and links are Gmail's own: pass them on unchanged.

agents.readme:
# Gmail (`gmail`)

Dana at Harbourline asks for a quotation for twenty desks. Ask the assistant to find her email, draft the reply with
the quotation PDF from the chat attached, and remind you on Thursday if she has not answered. The draft appears in
Gmail before it goes anywhere; the send needs your go-ahead; and Thursday's reminder fires only if the thread is still
quiet.

One or more Google accounts, connected by signing in: the platform runs the consent, keeps the refresh token and
refreshes it; the agent receives a short-lived access token and the address. `account_list` names them; every
function takes an optional `account` (the address, or a part of it that names one account only); a draft and a watch
remember the account they were made on.

## Functions

| Function | Level | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `account_status` | 0 | The connection, its address and the addresses it sends as |
| `account_list` | 0 | The connected accounts by address |
| `search_find` | 0 | Gmail's own query operators → one row per message, newest first, with thread id, labels and link |
| `search_thread` | 0 | A conversation whole: each part decoded by its own charset, HTML made readable when there is no text part, long bodies marked `truncated` with a `next_offset`; attachments listed by `part_id`, inline images left out |
| `search_message` | 0 | One message, or the rest of a long one, from `offset` |
| `search_save_attachment` | 0 | One attachment into the chat (at most 8 MiB − 64 KiB; a bigger one is refused before download, with a link) |
| `draft_compose` | 2 | A new message as a Gmail draft, with chat files attached and the send-as signature |
| `draft_reply` | 2 | A reply in the thread (`reply_all` keeps everyone and the Cc; the account itself is never a recipient), quoted |
| `draft_forward` | 2 | A forward with the original's attachments and any chat files |
| `draft_send` | 3 | Sends a prepared draft; succeeds only on Gmail's word; an unanswered send is `unknown` and never sent again |
| `draft_discard` | 2 | Deletes a draft this agent made; its text stays in the record |
| `mail_labels` | 0 | The labels |
| `mail_label` | 2 | Labels on or off conversations or messages; `create_missing` makes a new one |
| `mail_archive` | 2 | Out of the inbox |
| `mail_mark` | 2 | Read, unread, starred, unstarred, important, not important |
| `mail_trash` | 3 | To the trash (Gmail deletes it for good after 30 days) |
| `mail_restore` | 2 | Back out of the trash |
| `watch_await_reply` | 1 | Records that the user waits for a reply on a thread |
| `watch_check` | 1, schedulable | Unanswered and answered threads; a gone thread closes its watch |
| `watch_inbox` | 1 | Starts an inbox watch (from now, or from `since`); `only_from` / `skip_from` |
| `watch_new_mail` | 1, schedulable | What arrived since the last check, oldest first, every message once |
| `watches_list` | 0 | Every watch, both kinds |
| `watches_close` | 1 | Stops a watch for good |

Records: `draft` (what was prepared, in values, and what became of it), `watch` (threads awaited) and `inbox` (how far
the inbox has been read).

## Writing

A draft is one RFC 5322 message: `multipart/alternative` (the text, and the same text as escaped HTML with the
send-as signature), inside `multipart/mixed` when files are attached, each non-ASCII file name per RFC 2231. Each file
is at most a chat file's size, and all of them at most Gmail's 25 MB. A draft up to 1 MiB goes as JSON; a larger one
as a multipart upload to `/upload/gmail/v1/users/me/drafts` (Gmail takes at most 35 MB there). A reply sets the thread
id, `In-Reply-To`, `References` and the "Re:" subject, so Gmail keeps it in the conversation.

## Watching

A schedule runs `watch_check` and `watch_new_mail`, through the shared watch library: each watch is read on its own,
one that fails is listed in `problems` and keeps its place, and no cursor moves until every watch was read.

The inbox watch follows Gmail's history from a `startHistoryId`. Gmail keeps history for about a week, sometimes only
hours; when the id has expired (404), the watch reads the inbox again from the time of the last message it handed on,
through every page, and returns to history from the id the mailbox had before that reading. Nothing is skipped however
long the gap; a burst larger than `max_results` is handed on across checks. Mail from the account and its send-as
addresses never counts. Inbox watches made by 1.x go on from their time.

## What it will not do

Send, trash or forward on its own; delete mail for good; change Gmail settings or filters; bring a file larger than a
chat file into the chat. It needs `gmail.modify` and nothing more of Gmail.

agent.description: Google Calendar and Google Tasks, as Google's own app pairs them, for one or several Google accounts. See what is on in your own time zone, find a time when everyone is free on your working days, book with a Meet link, move, invite, answer or cancel; keep your Google Tasks lists, and hear what was completed or changed in them.
agent.instructions: Use this agent for Google Calendar and Google Tasks. Several accounts may be connected: pass account (the address) when the person names one; a refusal listing accounts means ask which. Start with account_status for the zone and today's date; resolve "tomorrow" or "Thursday" from that today, say the dates you took, and confirm before booking. Times without an offset are in the calendar's zone (or timezone). calendars_list shows every calendar; calendar_id defaults to primary. events_list expands recurring events; an all-day event's end is its last day. Attendees are email addresses: never guess one; ask, or take it from a mail thread. FINDING A TIME: events_find_times is code: it proposes only slots free for every calendar it could read and names the rest under unchecked; never call those free. Pass working_days (sunday..thursday in the Gulf; monday..friday is the default), working_hours, avoid and buffer_minutes as the person says. BOOKING: events_create is for the person's own calendar with nobody invited; events_book invites attendees (a proposal_ref, or start with end or duration_minutes), re-checks the slot first, and refuses if it was taken: offer another time, or book_anyway only when the person says so. meet adds a Google Meet link. send_updates is all unless the person says otherwise. Asking twice for the same booking finds the first (already: true), so an unknown result may be retried once. Invited is not accepted: events_get shows responses. events_update moves start and end together and keeps the length unless told. events_attendees adds or removes people. events_respond answers an invitation. events_cancel cancels when this account organises the event, otherwise declines it: tell the person which happened (done). TASKS: lists_list, then tasks_list (Google's own order; follow next_page_token). Due dates are YYYY-MM-DD only. A subtask is a task with parent. tasks_move moves within or between lists. tasks_delete cannot be undone. WATCHES: watches_create once per request (kind completed or changed, one list or every list), then schedule watches_check; it never reports this agent's own edits. watches_list and watches_close manage them. Never record a second watch for the same request.

agents.readme:
# Google Calendar (`google_calendar`) 2.0.0

Google Calendar and Google Tasks in one agent, as Google's own app pairs them. It absorbs `google_tasks` 1.0.0.

You need an hour with Dana next week, afternoons only, Sunday to Thursday. The assistant checks both calendars, says
whose calendar it could not see, and proposes slots. Pick one: it checks the slot is still free, books it with a Meet
link, and sends the invitation, which is the step you approve. Your Google Tasks sit beside it, and a schedule can tell
you each morning what was ticked off.

Same Google connection as every Google agent: connect an account once and grant it to each. Several accounts can be
connected; every function takes `account` (the address, or a part of it that names one).

## Functions

| Function | Level | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `account_status` | 0 | Each account: connected, its zone, today's date there, whether Tasks answers |
| `calendars_list` | 0 | Every calendar the account sees; `calendar_id` (default `primary`) picks one elsewhere |
| `events_list` | 0 | Events in a window (default today), in the calendar's zone or `timezone`; recurring ones expanded; Google's page tokens |
| `events_get` | 0 | One event with each attendee's real response |
| `events_availability` | 0 | Free/busy of the account's calendars and attendees; `unchecked` names calendars that can't be read |
| `events_find_times` | 1 | Slots computed in code: working days (Mon–Fri default, Sun–Thu possible), working hours, avoid windows, buffers; each kept as a proposal |
| `events_create` | 2 | An event on your own calendar with nobody invited (also all-day, repeating, shown as free) |
| `events_book` | 3 | A meeting with attendees from a proposal or a time; slot re-checked first; optional Meet link; `send_updates` all, externalOnly or none |
| `events_update` | 3 | Edit or move; start and end move together, the length kept unless told |
| `events_attendees` | 3 | Add or remove people |
| `events_respond` | 3 | Accept, decline or tentative |
| `events_cancel` | 3 | Cancel for everyone when you organise it, otherwise decline; says which (`done`) |
| `lists_list`, `lists_create` | 0, 2 | Task lists |
| `tasks_list`, `tasks_get` | 0 | Tasks a page at a time in your own order (any length); one task with its subtasks |
| `tasks_create`, `tasks_update`, `tasks_complete`, `tasks_reopen`, `tasks_move` | 2 | Changes you can undo; due dates are dates |
| `tasks_delete` | 3 | Deletes a task and its subtasks |
| `watches_create`, `watches_list`, `watches_close` | 1, 0, 1 | A watch on one list or every list, for `completed` or `changed` |
| `watches_check` | 1 | Schedulable: what each watch saw since last time, once; this agent's own edits left out |

Records: `proposal` (slots offered), `booking` (what this agent did to which event; the title and attendees
encrypted), `watch` (a cursor in Google's time).

## How it behaves

- **Zones.** A time without an offset is in the calendar's zone (read once per chat), or `timezone`. "Today" is today
  there, never in UTC.
- **Idempotent booking.** The event id is chosen from the request (or `request_id`), so asking twice, or after an
  answer was lost, finds the first event (`already: true`). A lost answer is looked up by that id before anything is
  sent again.
- **Watches** keep Google's time to the millisecond with the ids on that instant; a watch whose list is gone closes;
  one that fails keeps its place while the others are handed on; cursors are written once every watch was read.
- **Busy Google.** 429, and 403 `rateLimitExceeded`, are waited out (`Retry-After`), then reported as `rate`.

## What it will not do

Guess an attendee's address; call a calendar it could not read free; cancel someone else's meeting (it declines);
move an event it doesn't organise unless the organiser let guests modify it; send a level-3 change without approval.

## Limits, and what only a live account can confirm

The tests run the agent as its own program against a loopback Google (`tests/gcal_stub.py`) as strict as Google's
documented rules. Not yet verified live: free/busy keyed `primary` as asked; an attendee's response sent by patching
the whole attendee list; `destinationTasklist` moves; whether `updatedMin` is inclusive at the millisecond.
`find_times` looks at 31 days at most. Watches cover Google Tasks only, not calendar events.

agent.instructions: One agent for a person's Google Drive and the Docs, Sheets and Forms in it, across My Drive, shared drives and what was shared with them. Start with files_search (kind narrows it to document, spreadsheet, form, folder or pdf), files_list for a folder, or files_shared_with_me; every id comes from one of these, never invent one. files_drives lists shared drives. Several accounts may be connected: pass account (the address) when more than one is, and keep using it. Docs: docs_read gives numbered paragraphs across every tab, with headers, footers and footnotes; those numbers are what edits_propose and docs_insert take. Change a paragraph with edits_propose, show the old and new text, and only on a yes call edits_apply; it is refused if the document changed since. Sheets: sheets_get shows the tabs, sheets_read reads a window (from_row, max_rows) with the header row you name; continue with next_row, never re-reading the header. Uploads, folders, moves, copies, trash and restore change the person's drive; comments, invites and links are seen by others: ask before each. sharing_link shares within the organization unless the person asks for anyone with the link; a personal account has no organization, so ask. People are email addresses: ask for one rather than guess. Watches (changes_watch, comments_watch, rows_watch, responses_watch) are checked by the matching *_new function on a schedule; watches_list and watches_close manage them.

agents.readme:
# Google Drive (`google_drive`) 2.0.0

"Find the Riverside lease in our shared drive and bring me a PDF", "change the delivery paragraph of the Q3 proposal",
"add today's order to the Orders sheet", "how did people answer the feedback form?", "tell me every morning about new
sign-ups": one agent for a person's Google Drive, shared drives included, and the Docs, Sheets and Forms in it.

2.0.0 absorbs the Google Docs, Google Sheets and Google Forms agents (1.0.0), which are retired. It rides the same Google
connection as Gmail and Google Calendar: connect once, grant the saved account to each. Several accounts may be
connected; every function takes `account` (the address, or a part of it that names one account).

## Functions

| Function | Level | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `account_status` | 0 | Connected accounts; the address, organization (Google's `hd`) or personal, storage used |
| `account_connect` | 1 | Connect another Google account |
| `files_search` | 0 | Name or content, across My Drive and every shared drive (`corpora=allDrives`), by kind; paged |
| `files_list` | 0 | A folder by id (any drive) or path, folders first; paged |
| `files_shared_with_me` | 0 | Shared with the account, newest first, with who shared; paged |
| `files_drives` | 0 | The shared drives, with ids usable as folders |
| `files_get` | 0 | One item |
| `files_versions` | 0 | Earlier versions (revisions), newest first |
| `files_download` | 0 | A copy into the chat: a Google file exported (docx, xlsx, pptx, pdf, txt) or one tab as CSV with a BOM; refused before download over the chat's file limit, with the link |
| `files_upload` | 2 | A chat file into a folder: multipart up to 5 MB, a resumable session above; a free name, replace or fail; `convert` to a Google file |
| `files_create_folder`, `files_move`, `files_copy`, `files_trash`, `files_restore` | 2 | Filing; trash, never delete for good |
| `sharing_permissions` | 0 | Who can open it, each permission's id, inherited access marked |
| `sharing_invite` | 3 | People by address, read/comment/write; Google emails them unless `notify: false` |
| `sharing_link` | 3 | Within the account's organization (its hosted domain), or anyone when asked |
| `sharing_revoke` | 3 | One permission; never the owner's or inherited access |
| `changes_watch` / `changes_new` | 1 / 1, schedulable | Drive's change log from a start page token: all drives, one shared drive, or one folder |
| `docs_read` | 0 | Numbered paragraphs across every tab, with headers, footers and footnotes |
| `docs_create`, `docs_insert` | 2 | A new document; paragraphs added at the end or after one, refused if the doc changed since it was read |
| `edits_propose` / `edits_apply` / `edits_discard` | 1 / 2 / 1 | One paragraph's change as a record, then applied with `requiredRevisionId` |
| `comments_list` | 0 | A file's comments (open by default), paged without empty pages |
| `comments_add`, `comments_reply`, `comments_resolve` | 3 | Through the Drive comments API |
| `comments_watch` / `comments_new` | 1 / 1, schedulable | Others' new comments and replies |
| `sheets_get` | 0 | Tabs and grid sizes, locale, time zone |
| `sheets_read` | 0 | A window of rows; the header row named, read every time |
| `sheets_append`, `sheets_update` | 2 | RAW unless `formulas`; an overwrite keeps what was there |
| `sheets_create`, `sheets_add_tab` | 2 | A spreadsheet or a tab, with a header row |
| `sheets_find` | 0 | The cells holding a value |
| `sheets_totals` | 0 | Sum, count, min, max, average, by group: counted in code, in exact decimals |
| `rows_watch` / `rows_new` | 1 / 1, schedulable | New rows, seen even when a row is deleted and another added |
| `forms_get` | 0 | Questions, kinds, options |
| `responses_list` | 0 | Responses, paged with Google's own token |
| `responses_tally` | 0 | Per question: answered, each option's count, a scale's average; in code |
| `responses_watch` / `responses_new` | 1 / 1, schedulable | New responses |
| `watches_list`, `watches_close` | 0, 1 | Every watch of the four kinds |

Records: `share` (grants and revocations), `edit` (proposed document changes; their text encrypted in values),
`write` (sheet writes, with what an overwrite replaced), `watch` (one per watch, its cursor in keys).

## Rules it keeps

- **Shared drives everywhere.** `supportsAllDrives` on every request that names a file; listings say
  `includeItemsFromAllDrives` and the right `corpora`.
- **Busy Google is waited out.** 429 and 403 `rateLimitExceeded`/`userRateLimitExceeded` are tried again after
  `Retry-After` (the shared `standard.google`); a missing permission says to reconnect.
- **The chat's file limit.** 8 MiB less 64 KiB. A file Drive says is bigger is refused before a byte is read; an export
  (which states no size) is cut off while it streams. Google exports at most 10 MB.
- **Uploads the way Google asks:** multipart up to 5 MB, resumable above.
- **A link stays in the organization** named by the account's hosted domain, never guessed from the address. A
  personal account has none and is told so; "anyone with the link" is only on request.
- **Documents:** read with `includeTabsContent=true`; edits and inserts sent with `requiredRevisionId`, so a document
  changed in between is refused by Google, never overwritten. A paragraph holding an image, a chip or a footnote mark
  is not rewritten.
- **Sheets:** a read is a window, never the whole tab; the header row is the one named, never a continued read's first
  row. Writes are `RAW` unless the person asks for formulas, so "=IMPORTDATA(…)" pasted from an email stays text. Sums
  and counts are made in code.
- **Forms:** the tally is counted in code; pages are Google's own.
- **Watches** (`standard.watch`): each read alone; one that fails keeps its cursor and is named in `problems`; a gone
  file, tab, form or shared drive closes its watch; cursors are written only once every watch was read.

## Limits, and what only a live account can confirm

Verified against a loopback stub (`tests/gdrive_stub.py`) as strict as Google's documented rules; the first real
connection is the first live run. Not yet seen live: whether `alt=media` downloads redirect (to
`*.googleusercontent.com`, declared in case); the exact error for an export over 10 MB; that the Forms `filter`
compares `lastSubmittedTime`; that `changes.list` without `driveId` reports shared-drive changes with
`includeItemsFromAllDrives`; that `oauth2/v3/userinfo` gives `hd` with the `openid email` scopes; the exact status for a
stale `requiredRevisionId` (handled as a 400 naming the revision, or `FAILED_PRECONDITION`).

The `drive`, `documents` and `spreadsheets` scopes are restricted or sensitive Google scopes: a public app needs Google's
verification before people outside its test users can connect.

agent.name: Mail
agent.description: Any mail account, read and answered through the assistant: Gmail, Yahoo, iCloud, Fastmail, or a mail server of your own. Connect it with its address and an app password. Find a conversation, read it whole, draft a reply, a reply to all or a forward, with files from the chat attached, and see it before anything is sent; sending is a separate step you approve; a watch reminds you only while a reply is still missing; and an inbox watch, run on a schedule, reports only the mail that arrived.
agent.instructions: Use this agent to find, read, answer, forward or follow up on email in an account connected here with its address and an app password. Several accounts may be connected: account_list names them, and every function takes an optional account (the address); pass it when the user names an inbox or the agent says several are connected. Drafts and watches remember their account. Always find the conversation first (search_find, then search_thread) and quote what it actually says; never invent a message, a sender, a date or an id. search_find takes no query language: a sender in from, a recipient in to, subject words in subject, words anywhere in query, dates in since and before (2026-09-03); all empty is the newest mail. It reads one folder: the archive of everything where there is one, else the inbox; folder sent for what the user sent, or any folder by the name folders_list shows. A reply (draft_reply; reply_all copies everyone on the message answered), a new message (draft_compose) or a forward (draft_forward) is prepared as a DRAFT and shown to the user before anything is sent; attachments takes files from the chat. draft_send is a separate external action that needs the user's explicit go-ahead. A send that comes back "unknown" was handed to the mail server and not confirmed: say so and do not send again; the user should check the Sent folder. A refused send sent nothing; the draft stays ready. To be reminded when a conversation has not been answered, record a watch (watch_await_reply) and schedule watch_check. To act on mail as it arrives, record an inbox watch ONCE (watch_inbox, narrowed with only_from / skip_from when the user names senders) and schedule watch_new_mail every few minutes; each run returns only what arrived since the last check, with its thread_id. Never record a second inbox watch for the same request; watches_list and watches_close show and stop watches. Pass on any problems or notices a run reports. Message and thread ids are the messages' own: pass them on unchanged. When a sign-in is refused, the problem says where the user makes an app password; pass that on as it is.

functions.name: Send Draft
functions.description: Send a prepared draft. An external, irreversible action: only on the user's explicit go-ahead. Succeeds only when the mail server takes the message; an unconfirmed outcome is reported as unknown and is never retried here; a refusal sends nothing and leaves the draft ready. A copy is put in the account's Sent folder where the server kept none itself.

functions.name: Discard Draft
functions.description: Mark a prepared draft discarded. It is never sent.

functions.description: Check every waiting watch (or one, by watch_ref) against the mailbox. "unanswered" lists the conversations still without a reply from someone other than the account — empty once all were answered. A watch that could not be checked is in problems and is checked again next time; one whose conversation is gone is closed. Schedulable: on a cadence, a run has something to report only while a reply is still missing.

functions.name: Watch The Inbox
functions.description: Start watching the inbox for new mail. LEAVE "since" EMPTY to start from now, which is almost always what is meant. A "since" is only for starting in the past, and must carry its UTC offset (2026-09-20T17:51:00+04:00): a time without one is read as UTC, not as the person's zone, and one in the future is taken as now. Optionally count only some senders: only_from / skip_from take addresses or "@domain"s, comma-separated. Record it once, then schedule watch_new_mail.

functions.name: New Mail
functions.description: What arrived in the inbox since the last check, for every inbox watch (or one, by inbox_ref): one row per message, oldest first, shaped like search_find, each naming its watch. Mail from the account itself and from senders the watch leaves out is not reported. Moves the watch forward; "more" says a later check continues; problems lists a watch that could not be read (it keeps its place); notices says when the server renumbered the inbox. Schedulable: a run with nothing in "messages" has nothing to report.

functions.name: List Watches
functions.description: Every reply watch and inbox watch, by ref and kind; waiting and watching ones unless include_closed.

functions.name: Stop a Watch
functions.description: Stop a reply watch or an inbox watch for good; a scheduled check hears nothing more from it.

agents.readme:
# Mail (`mail`)

Someone wants the assistant to read their mail and has never heard of
a developer console. They type their address and an app password, and
ask for the latest message from a supplier.

Any mail account, over the protocols mail has always spoken: read over
IMAP, sent over SMTP, both encrypted, from where this agent runs to
the account's own mail server. Nothing is registered with a provider
and nobody reviews anything.

It does what the Gmail and Outlook agents do, and the assistant uses
the three alike.

## Connecting an account

| Field | What goes in it |
|---|---|
| Email address | the account's address |
| Provider | `gmail`, `yahoo`, `icloud`, `fastmail`, or `other` |
| App password | a password made in the provider's security settings for one program to use — not the account's own, which most providers refuse here |
| IMAP server, SMTP server | for `other` only: the provider's mail servers, each with its port, as `imap.example.com:993` and `smtp.example.com:465` (or `:587`) |

| Provider | Where an app password is made |
|---|---|
| Gmail | 2-Step Verification on, then `https://myaccount.google.com/apppasswords` |
| Yahoo | Account security, Generate app password |
| iCloud | `https://account.apple.com`, Sign-In and Security, App-Specific Passwords |
| Fastmail | Settings, Privacy & Security, App passwords |

Microsoft's accounts are not here: Outlook.com takes no password over
IMAP, and the Outlook agent is the way in.

More than one account can be connected. `account_list` names them, and
every function that reads or writes mail takes an optional `account`
(the address, or a part of it). Left out, the only one answers; none
yet, and the person is asked to connect one; several is refused, with
their names. A draft, a watch and an inbox watch keep the account they
were made on.

## Functions

| Function | Level | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `account_status` | 0 | Signs in and opens the inbox; when that fails, says why and where an app password is made |
| `account_list` | 0 | The connected accounts, by address |
| `folders_list` | 0 | Every folder by name, in any alphabet, with what it is (sent, drafts, trash, junk, all), and counts if asked |
| `search_find` | 0 | Messages in one folder, newest first: by sender, recipient, subject, words anywhere, dates, unread |
| `search_thread` | 0 | One conversation whole, from the inbox and from what was sent, with its attachments listed |
| `search_save_attachment` | 0 | One attachment, handed to the chat as a file (at most 8 MB less 64 KB, the most a chat file can be) |
| `draft_reply`, `draft_compose`, `draft_forward` | 1 | A draft (a reply, a reply to all, a new message, a forward with the message's attachments), with files from the chat attached; kept by the platform and shown to the person. Nothing is sent |
| `draft_send` | 3 | Sends a draft, on the person's go-ahead. `sent` only when the mail server took it; `unknown` when its bytes went and no answer came, and never tried again; a refusal sends nothing and leaves the draft ready |
| `draft_discard` | 1 | Marks a draft discarded |
| `watch_await_reply`, `watch_check` | 1 | Remembers a conversation and says whether somebody else has written since. `watch_check` is schedulable |
| `watch_inbox`, `watch_new_mail` | 1 | Remembers how far the inbox was read and hands on what arrived since, once. `watch_new_mail` is schedulable |
| `watches_list`, `watches_close` | 0, 1 | Every watch of either kind, and stopping one for good |

Drafts (their words and recipients encrypted), the files attached to them, reply watches and inbox watches are
records.

## How it keeps its word

- **Off the agent's loop.** Every socket, IMAP and SMTP call runs in a thread, so a slow mail server never stalls the
  chat's other calls.
- **Sent once.** A draft is claimed before its first byte goes, in the process and in its record (`sending`). Its
  Message-ID is chosen when it is drafted. A refusal at any step before the message's bytes (the sign-in, the
  sender, a recipient, DATA itself) or after them sends nothing, and the draft stays ready; only bytes that went with
  no answer are `unknown`.
- **Written to pass any server:** 7-bit (base64 or quoted-printable bodies, RFC 2047 headers), the server's SIZE
  held to, an attachment's name in another alphabet written per RFC 2231.
- **Read as written:** RFC 2047 headers and raw 8-bit ones (UTF-8, else Windows-1256 or -1252); folder names in
  IMAP's modified UTF-7, both ways; a snippet from the first text part, asked of the server by its structure, and for
  HTML only its words.
- **Watches never lose mail.** Each is read on its own (`standard.watch`): one that fails is listed in `problems` and
  keeps its place; a conversation that is gone closes its watch; a reply watch whose last message disappeared goes by
  that message's time; an inbox the server renumbered (a new UIDVALIDITY) is read by arrival time, and the run says
  so in `notices`.

## What differs from Gmail's own agent

- **No query language.** `search_find` takes a sender, a subject, words and dates as separate inputs.
- **One folder a search.** The account's archive of everything where it has one (Gmail's All Mail), else the inbox;
  `folder: sent` for what was sent, or any folder by the name `folders_list` shows.
- **A conversation is rebuilt.** A mail server keeps messages, not conversations: a conversation is the messages that
  name one another in `References` or `In-Reply-To`, followed both ways. Ids are the messages' own `Message-ID`s.
- **A draft lives on the platform,** not in the account's Drafts folder: what is sent is what the person was shown.
- **A copy of what was sent** is put in the Sent folder where the server kept none itself.
- **No link to a message:** a mail server has no web page for one.

## Where it connects

The mail servers of the four providers it knows by name, each on the
port mail is read on (993) and the ports it is sent on (465, 587;
iCloud only 587), and for another provider the servers the account
names (`from_secret`).
Every connection is opened with the standard's `Tunnel`, through the
sandbox's way out, which opens those hosts on those ports and nothing
else. The way out passes the bytes and reads none of them: the
connection is encrypted between this agent and the mail server.

**A server the account names is reached on the port written with it.**
The standard's `from_secret` names a field, not a port, and the way out
opens the host read from it on the web's ports (80, 443) only, unless
the field's value itself is `host:port`. So for another provider the
servers are written with their ports (`imap.example.com:993`,
`smtp.example.com:465`), and the agent connects on the port written
there. A server written without one is tried on mail's own ports, as
before (993; 465, then 587), which the way out refuses: the refusal
says to write the port.

## What it never does

It deletes no mail, moves none and marks none as read: folders are
opened to be read. The one thing it writes to a mailbox is the copy of
what it sent.

agent.instructions: Use this agent to find, read and write pages and databases in the person's Notion workspace. It sees only the pages the person shared with the integration; when Notion says something is not shared or not found, tell the person to share that page with the integration (the page's ... menu, then Connections) or to reconnect and select it, and do not guess another id.
