agents.readme:
# Notion (`notion`)

"Which office move tasks are still in progress, who has them, and what does the launch plan still have open?"
Pages are found by title, read as text, and queried with filters. You can add a task, assign it, tick a status,
append a checklist, trash a page or leave a comment. Each change waits for your go-ahead, is checked against the
database's own schema first, and is kept on record.

The agent works on one or more Notion workspaces through the Notion API. It sees only what the person shared with the
integration while signing in. A page it cannot open is a page to share, and its errors say so.

## Functions

Every function takes an optional `account` (the workspace's address) when several workspaces are connected.

| Function | Level | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `account_status` | 0 | The connection, the workspace's name and the integration's. Asks nobody |
| `search_find` | 0 | Pages and databases (their data sources) by title, newest edited first; paged |
| `pages_read` | 0 | A page's properties as text, and its body as one line per block, a window at a time |
| `databases_get` | 0 | A database's schema: property names, types, options. For a database of several data sources, lists them |
| `databases_query` | 0 | Rows with properties as text; one simple filter or a compound `filter` (all/any, nested once), a sort; paged |
| `pages_create` | 2 | A row, validated against its data source's schema, or a page under a page; optional paragraphs |
| `pages_update` | 2 | Changes a row's properties (or a page's title); records what each was before |
| `pages_archive` | 2 | Moves a page or row to Notion's trash, or restores it with `restore` |
| `blocks_append` | 2 | Adds paragraphs, to-dos and bullets to the end of a page |
| `comments_list` | 0 | A page's comments |
| `comments_add` | 3 | A page-level comment, shown as written by the integration and seen by others at once |
| `watch_database` | 1 | Records a watch on a database, from now in Notion's clock |
| `watch_changes` | 1, schedulable | Rows created or edited since the last check, for every watch; each watch read on its own |
| `watches_list` | 0 | The watches, with what each follows and how far it was read |
| `watches_close` | 1 | Stops a watch for good |

Records: `write` holds every page, row, property change, trash, block append and comment this agent made, with the
previous values of an update. `watch` holds the databases followed and how far each was read.

## Notion's API version, and data sources

Every request carries `Notion-Version: 2026-03-11`. Since 2025-09-03 a database is a container of one or more data
sources. The schema and the rows belong to a data source (`data_sources/{id}`, `data_sources/{id}/query`), and a new
row's parent is `{type: data_source_id}`. `database_id` takes either id: a data source's (what a search returns) or a
database's (what a link copied from Notion holds). A database with one data source is that source. One with several is
refused with each source named, so the person can say which. 2026-03-11 also renamed the trash flag to `in_trash`;
`archived` is no longer sent.

## Rules it keeps

- **Nothing in the workspace changes without a yes.** Writes the person can undo (create, update, trash, append) are
  level 2. A comment, which others see at once, is level 3.
- **The schema decides what a row may hold.** A property that does not exist, or an option that is not defined, is
  refused with the valid ones named. Notion would silently add a new select option; this agent does not. Computed
  properties (formulas, rollups, created time, unique ids) and files are refused.
- **People by name or address.** A people property (an assignee) takes names, addresses or user ids, matched against
  the workspace's own people. A name that matches no one, or several people, is refused, and the refusal names who can be chosen.
- **Numbers are exact.** `12.50` is sent as `12.50`, never through a float. A decimal comma ("1,250") is refused
  rather than guessed at.
- **Long or non-Latin text is split where Notion allows.** A rich-text piece holds at most 2,000 UTF-16 units, and the
  agent never cuts an emoji or an Arabic letter with its marks.
- **Update keeps the before.** `pages_update` returns and records each changed property's previous value.
- **Nothing is invented.** Page, data source and comment ids come from a search, a query or a page read.
- **Results stay small.** At most 25 rows per call (20 by default). A page is read at most 100 blocks at a time, with
  `from`, `next_from` and a `total`. A block's text is clipped at 2,000 characters and a property's at 500.

## Following a database

1. `watch_database {database_id}` returns a `watch_ref`.
2. The assistant schedules `watch_changes`. It runs with no model.
3. Each row says whether it was `created` or `edited`, and which watch it belongs to. `more: true` means a later check
   continues. A watch that failed (a database no longer shared, say) is listed in `problems` and keeps its place. Its
   rows come on the next run, and the other watches are not held back. A watch whose database was deleted or trashed
   closes itself and is listed in `closed`.

Notion keeps `last_edited_time` to the minute. The cursor is the newest minute handed on, plus the ids of the rows seen
on that minute. The ids are kept encrypted in `values` as an object, so a busy minute cannot overflow a field. A second
edit to a row within the minute it was already reported in carries the same time. That edit surfaces with the row's
next edit in a later minute.

Watches kept by 1.0.0 (status `watching`, a `seen` string) go on where they were. Their data source is looked up once,
and their seen ids move to `values`.

## Errors

| kind | when |
|---|---|
| `auth` | the token was revoked or has expired: reconnect the workspace |
| `denied` | Notion answered 403 `restricted_resource`: share the page with the integration (••• menu, Connections) |
| `not_found` | Notion answered 404: no such id, or not shared (Notion does not tell these apart, so the same hint is given) |
| `rate` | Notion stayed busy (429 or 529) past the wait the agent allows; the words say Notion's Retry-After |
| `conflict` | Notion reported a conflicting change; read again and retry |
| `unknown` | a write got no answer: whether it was done is unknown, and it is never sent again |
| `invalid` | refused before sending (an unknown property, option or person, a bad date or number), or by Notion |

A 429 is waited out as Notion's `Retry-After` says, up to 30 seconds in all, for reads and writes alike, since a
refused request did nothing.

## Setup

Once per organization, by an administrator, at [notion.so/my-integrations](https://www.notion.so/my-integrations):

1. Create a new integration of type **Public**.
2. Capabilities: **Read content**, **Update content**, **Insert content**, **Read comments**, **Insert comments**, and
   **Read user information including email addresses**. Assigning people and naming the account both need it.
3. Add the redirect URI DecentAI shows under **Settings → Connected apps**.
4. Copy the OAuth client id and secret into DecentAI as provider `notion`.

Then, per workspace: **Agents → Notion → Credentials → Connect account**, and choose the pages to share.

## Limits

- Titles only: Notion's search does not look inside page text.
- Comments are page-level; comment authors are user ids, not names.
- A page's total is counted up to 1,000 top-level blocks; a block's children up to 100.
- People are matched among the first 1,000 people of the workspace.
- Tested against a loopback stub of the API subset it uses. The first real connection is the first live run.

agent.name: OneDrive
agent.description: Your OneDrive, work or personal, and the Word, Excel and Forms files in it, through the assistant. Find, fetch, file and share files; read a Word document and change it on your go-ahead; read and add to Excel tables; read a form's responses; and hear when a document, a table or a form changes.
agent.instructions:
Use this agent for a person's OneDrive and the Word, Excel and Forms files in it, on a work or school (Microsoft 365) or a personal Microsoft account. Start with files_search (by name or content; it finds files others shared too), files_list (a folder) or files_shared_with_me. Take item_id from a result, and drive_id whenever the result has one (a shared file lives in its owner's drive), and pass both on; never invent an id, a worksheet or a table name. With several accounts connected, pass account (the address).
Files: files_download brings a copy into the chat (at most 8 MB; a bigger file is refused with its link, which you give the person). files_upload puts a chat file into a folder (renamed on a clash unless the person says replace). Uploading, creating folders, moving, renaming, copying and deleting change the person's drive: ask first. Several items to one folder: one files_move_many. files_copy may finish later: pass its monitor to files_copy_status. Delete goes to the recycle bin; files_restore brings it back on a personal account only.
Sharing (others see it; always ask): look with sharing_permissions first. sharing_invite takes email addresses, never names: find the address first. If it answers emailed false, tell the person Microsoft sent no email and give them the link to send. sharing_link makes an organization-only link on a work account; a link for anyone with it (link_scope anonymous) only when the person asks for that in those words. A personal account has no organization link: ask what they want.
Word: word_find, then word_read (numbered paragraphs a slice at a time; continue with next_from) and word_comments (read only: this agent cannot add, answer or resolve comments). To change text call word_propose with the paragraph number and the whole new text of that paragraph, show old and new side by side, and only on the go-ahead word_apply. Refused because the document changed: read it again and propose afresh, never retry the old edit. Locked: someone has it open; try later. Unknown: ask the person to look at the document.
Excel (work or school accounts): excel_find, excel_get (the worksheets and tables really there), excel_rows (a table's rows keyed by header), excel_read (a block by A1 address; say when rows_cut or columns_cut shows it was capped). excel_add_rows and excel_write change the workbook: show what excel_write will replace before asking. Text starting with = is written as text unless the person asks for a formula (formulas true).
Forms (work or school accounts): forms_find finds the workbook a form's responses sync to; forms_responses reads them newest first. Times are ISO, in the time Excel shows, with no zone.
Watches: to hear about a document's saves and comments, a table's new rows or a form's new responses, make the watch once (watches_document, watches_rows, watches_responses) and schedule watches_check; each check returns only what is new. Tell the person about anything in problems, closed or reset. watches_list shows the watches; watches_close stops one.
An "unsupported" answer means the feature needs another kind of account: say which, in a sentence.

functions.description: One file or folder's details, by item_id (and drive_id for a shared one).

agents.readme:
# OneDrive (`onedrive`) 2.0.0

"Where is the Riverside lease, and who can open it?" — found by name or content, in your drive or among what others
shared with you, with everyone who has access. Bring a copy into the chat; file a chat file into a folder; share it
with Dana. Read the Harbourline proposal paragraph by paragraph with its comments, and change one paragraph on your
go-ahead. Read and add to an Excel table; read a form's responses from the workbook it syncs to; and hear each morning
what changed.

One agent for a Microsoft account's OneDrive, work or school (Microsoft 365) or personal (outlook.com), and the Word,
Excel and Forms files in it. It replaces Word Online, Excel Online and Microsoft Forms (1.x), whose watches must be
made again here. It rides the same Microsoft connection as every Microsoft agent; several accounts may be connected,
and every function takes an optional `account`.

## Functions

| Function | Level | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `account_status` | 0 | Each connected account, its drive's kind (personal or business), how full it is |
| `files_search` | 0 | Files and folders by name or content, shared ones included (with their `drive_id`) |
| `files_list` | 0 | A folder, by path or id, a page at a time |
| `files_shared_with_me` | 0 | What others shared; Microsoft's retiring list, filled in by search |
| `files_get` / `files_versions` | 0 | One item's details; its earlier versions |
| `files_download` | 0 | A copy into the chat (at most 8 MB; bigger is refused with its link); Office files as PDF |
| `files_upload` | 2 | A chat file into a folder: one request under 4 MiB, an upload session above; renamed on a clash |
| `files_create_folder`, `files_move`, `files_move_many`, `files_copy` | 2 | Folders, moves and renames, copies (followed until done) |
| `files_copy_status` | 0 | A copy's progress |
| `files_delete` / `files_restore` | 2 | To the recycle bin; back from it (personal accounts) |
| `sharing_permissions` | 0 | Who can open an item, and how |
| `sharing_invite`, `sharing_link`, `sharing_revoke` | 3 | Share with people, make a link, stop sharing; each recorded |
| `word_find`, `word_read`, `word_comments` | 0 | Word documents, by paragraph, with their comments |
| `word_propose` / `word_discard` | 1 | Record (or drop) a change to one paragraph |
| `word_apply` | 2 | Save it, only if the document's content is unchanged since |
| `excel_find`, `excel_get`, `excel_read`, `excel_rows` | 0 | Workbooks, their sheets and tables, blocks and rows |
| `excel_write`, `excel_add_rows` | 2 | Cells (several blocks in one session) and table rows; each recorded |
| `forms_find`, `forms_responses` | 0 | A form's responses from the workbook it syncs to |
| `watches_document`, `watches_rows`, `watches_responses` | 1 | Watch a document, a table, a form |
| `watches_check` | 1 | Schedulable: what is new in every watch, once |
| `watches_list` / `watches_close` | 0 / 1 | The watches; stop one |

Records: `share` (every grant and revocation), `edit` (Word edits), `write` (workbook writes, with what the cells
held), `watch`. What people wrote, and who a file was shared with, are kept encrypted (`values`).

## Rules it keeps

- **Downloads never carry the token.** Graph hands each file a pre-authenticated address on another host
  (SharePoint, `*.files.1drv.com`, `my.microsoftpersonalcontent.com`, `*-mediap.svc.ms` for PDF); every such host is
  declared, and fetched without the Authorization header. Upload sessions likewise.
- **A shared file is reached in its owner's drive** (`drive_id` with `item_id`), never as one of yours.
- **Changes in your own drive are level 2; anything others see is level 3.** A link is for your organization unless
  you ask for "anyone with the link"; a personal account has no organization links and is told so.
- **An invitation Microsoft will not email** (it happens on personal accounts) still grants access, and you are told
  to send the link yourself.
- **A Word edit is saved only if the content is unchanged** (the cTag: a rename does not count), with `If-Match`;
  a document open elsewhere is reported as locked, and the edit waits.
- **Text that looks like a formula is written as text** unless you ask for a formula.
- **Excel and Forms need a work or school account**: Microsoft's workbook API does not exist for personal ones.
- **Watches never lose what they read**: each is read alone, a failing one keeps its place, a gone file closes its
  watch.

## Will not

- Add, answer or resolve Word comments; edit a paragraph holding tracked changes, a picture or an equation.
- Browse SharePoint site libraries other than files shared with you; list the recycle bin.
- Bring a file over 8 MB into the chat.

Tested against a loopback Graph as strict as Microsoft's documented rules; see the first-live-run list in the
release notes for what only a real account can confirm.

agent.name: Outlook
agent.description: Your Microsoft 365 or Outlook.com mail, calendar and To Do, through the assistant. Read whole conversations and attachments, draft replies, forwards and new mail with files attached and send only on your go-ahead; see your calendar, find a time that suits everyone, and invite, move, cancel or answer meetings; keep your To Do lists; and be told when a reply arrives, new mail lands or a task is ticked off.
agent.instructions: Use this agent for a Microsoft 365 or Outlook.com account's mail, calendar and To Do. account_list names the connected accounts; every function takes an optional account (the address): pass it when the person names one or when several are connected. account_status says the account's addresses, whether it is work or personal, its time zone and today's date. MAIL. For "what came in" or unread mail start with mail_list; to find something, mail_find (Microsoft's search words: from:, subject:, received>=2026-09-01, hasattachments:true). Then read before answering: mail_thread for a conversation, mail_read for one message. Quote what the mail says; never invent a message, sender, date or id. If a result has "next" (thread) or next_offset (message), there is more: call again before saying what it says. Attachments are listed with each message; mail_save_attachment brings one into the chat for another agent to read. A reply (draft_reply; all true to reply to all), a forward (draft_forward) or a new message (draft_compose) is prepared as a DRAFT, chat files attached with files, and shown to the person; draft_send is a separate step that needs their explicit go-ahead. A send that comes back "unknown" was not confirmed: say so, never send again; they should look in Sent Items. mail_mark, mail_move, mail_archive and mail_folders keep mail in order. CALENDAR. Start with calendar_list (dates in the person's zone; it says today's date). To find a time, calendar_find_times: it proposes only slots free for everyone whose calendar could be checked and names the others in unchecked; never present those as free. Book a slot with calendar_invite and its proposal_ref, or calendar_create for an event with nobody invited. Attendees are email addresses: take them from mail or ask; never guess one. Inviting, changing, cancelling and answering (calendar_respond) are seen by others and need the person's go-ahead. When a date is ambiguous ("Thursday"), say which date you took. calendar_cancel on someone else's meeting declines it. TASKS. Start with tasks_list (the default To Do list unless list is named; tasks_lists names them). Add, change, complete and reopen freely; tasks_delete needs a go-ahead. Due dates are YYYY-MM-DD in the person's zone. WATCHES. Record a watch once, then schedule its check: watch_reply then watch_check (reminders while a reply is missing); watch_inbox then watch_new_mail (act on new mail as the person's standing instruction says); watch_tasks then watch_task_changes (what was ticked off in To Do). watches_list shows them, watches_close stops one. Never record a second watch for the same request. Some features need a work or school account (other people's free/busy, Teams links); on a personal account the agent says so. Ids and links are Outlook's own: pass them on unchanged.

agents.readme:
# Outlook (`outlook`)

Dana at Harbourline asks for a quotation for twenty desks. Ask the assistant to read her whole conversation, draft the
reply with the price list attached, find an hour next week when both of you are free, and add "chase Dana" to your To Do
list. Nothing is sent, booked or deleted until you say so.

One agent for a Microsoft 365 (work or school) or Outlook.com (personal) account: mail, calendar and Microsoft To Do.
Version 2.0.0 absorbs the Microsoft Calendar and Microsoft To Do agents.

The platform runs the sign-in, keeps the refresh token and hands the agent a short-lived access token and the address.
A person may connect several accounts: `account_list` names them, every function takes an optional `account`, and a
draft, a proposal and a watch remember the account they were made on.

## Functions

| Function | Level | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `account_list`, `account_status` | 0 | The connected accounts; one's addresses, work or personal, time zone and today's date |
| `mail_list` | 0 | A folder's newest mail, optionally unread only, from one sender, since a date |
| `mail_find` | 0 | Microsoft's search (`from:`, `subject:`, `received>=`), newest first; `page_token` continues |
| `mail_thread` | 0 | A whole conversation, each message's own words, its attachments; paged with `next`, never cut |
| `mail_read` | 0 | One message whole, the HTML read as text; a long body in parts (`next_offset`) |
| `mail_save_attachment` | 0 | A file attachment, or an attached message as `.eml`, into the chat (at most 8 MiB less 64 KiB) |
| `mail_folders` | 0 | Folders with their paths and counts |
| `mail_mark`, `mail_move`, `mail_archive` | 2 | Read/unread and flags; moving to a folder by name or path; the Archive folder |
| `draft_compose`, `draft_reply`, `draft_forward` | 2 | Outlook drafts: new, reply or reply to all (the quoted history kept), forward; chat files attached |
| `draft_attach` | 2 | More chat files on a prepared draft (under 3 MB in one request, larger in an upload session) |
| `draft_send` | 3 | Sends a draft; succeeds only when Outlook confirms it left Drafts, otherwise "unknown" and never resent |
| `draft_discard` | 2 | The draft to Deleted Items |
| `calendar_list`, `calendar_get`, `calendar_calendars` | 0 | What is on (recurring meetings expanded, all-day events as days, any calendar), one event whole |
| `calendar_availability` | 0 | Busy periods of the account and of others |
| `calendar_find_times` | 1 | Free slots on working days, kept as proposals |
| `calendar_create` | 2 | An event of your own, nobody invited |
| `calendar_invite`, `calendar_update`, `calendar_cancel`, `calendar_respond` | 3 | Invitations (a Teams link on work accounts), changes, cancelling (or declining someone else's), answers |
| `tasks_lists`, `tasks_list`, `tasks_get` | 0 | To Do lists and tasks; due and completed dates in your zone |
| `tasks_create`, `tasks_update`, `tasks_complete`, `tasks_reopen`, `tasks_create_list` | 2 | Changes to tasks you can undo |
| `tasks_delete` | 3 | A task deleted for good |
| `watch_reply` / `watch_check` | 1 / 1, schedulable | A reminder while a reply is missing |
| `watch_inbox` / `watch_new_mail` | 1 / 1, schedulable | New mail in a folder, once each |
| `watch_tasks` / `watch_task_changes` | 1 / 1, schedulable | What was ticked off (or changed) in To Do, from its own change feed |
| `watches_list`, `watches_close` | 0, 1 | Every watch; stopping one |

## How it reads

- **Whole conversations.** A thread is read by its conversation id, ordered here (Graph refuses a filter on one property
  with an order on another). Each message comes with its own words (`uniqueBody`), the quoted history being the
  messages before it; `quoted: true` gives every body whole. When the size runs out the result says `complete: false`
  and `next` names where to go on.
- **Text from HTML.** Outlook is asked for text bodies; an HTML body that still arrives is turned into text here.
- **Attachments** are listed by kind (file, attached item, cloud link); inline pictures such as a signature's logo are
  left out.
- **Who is "me".** Every address of the account counts as its own: the mail address, the sign-in name and the aliases.

## Time

The person's zone is the `timezone` input, else the mailbox's own (read from its settings, a Windows name mapped through
the whole of CLDR's table), else UTC, and the result says which. Working days are the mailbox's own, or `working_days`
(Sunday to Thursday works), else Monday to Friday. Due dates are written as their midnight in the person's zone;
completions are dated by the person's day.

## Personal accounts

Other people's free/busy and Teams meeting links need a work or school account; on Outlook.com the agent says so before
writing anything. Finding a time on a personal account reads the account's own calendar and names the others as
unchecked.

## What it will not do

- Send, invite, cancel, answer an invitation or delete a task without your go-ahead.
- Send a draft twice after an unconfirmed send.
- Bring a file larger than 8 MiB less 64 KiB into the chat: it gives the message's link instead.
- Read a shared mailbox, or other people's calendars beyond free/busy.
- Report a completion again because a done task was edited.

agents.readme:
# Places and Distances (`places`)

You are meeting a client near Dubai Marina tomorrow morning. Ask for a
quiet coffee place that is open, its hours and phone number, and how
long the drive is from the office at 8am. The assistant answers from
Google Maps — every name, address, rating and time is Google's — and
says the travel time is Google's estimate at the moment it asked.

Finds places by text or near a point, reads one place's address,
phone, website and opening hours, and estimates distance and travel
time from one origin to many destinations. Google Maps Platform over
the organization's API key: Places API (New) and Routes API. Every
function is a read; nothing is kept.

## Functions

| Function | Level | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `account_status` | 0 | Confirms the key works for each API at no cost; names the API to enable, or the problem, when it does not |
| `places_search` | 0 | Free-text search ("coffee near Dubai Marina"), optional location bias and `open_now`; up to 20 rows |
| `places_nearby` | 0 | Places of given types within a radius of a point or a place, nearest first; up to 20 rows |
| `places_details` | 0 | One place: address, location, business status, Maps link; hours, open now, phone, website, rating or price when `include` names them |
| `routes_distance` | 0 | One origin to up to 20 destinations: km, minutes, minutes in traffic when driving at a stated time, directions link |
| `routes_between` | 0 | One trip with its summary (main road), Google's warnings and the first 20 steps; for transit each ride's line, vehicle, stops, times and the fare |

None is schedulable, and none keeps a record.

**Cheap by default.** A row carries id, name, address, location and a
Maps link: Google's Pro tier. Rating, price, open now, hours, phone and
website are Enterprise fields and are asked only when the function's
`include` names them; each answer says the `tier` it was billed at.
`open_now: true` as a search *filter* adds no field.

**Language and region.** `language` (BCP-47, such as `ar`) and `region`
(two letters, such as `AE`) are sent as Google's `languageCode` and
`regionCode`. Left out, the language is taken from the script the person
wrote in (Arabic script → `ar`, or `fa`/`ur` when their letters say so)
and the region from the `timezone` input (`Asia/Dubai` → `AE`); Latin
text with no zone sends neither, and Google decides. Routes takes the
region as a ccTLD (`uk` for GB); the agent converts it.

A row carries only what Google returned: a place with no rating has no
`rating`, never a zero. `straight_line_km` in `places_nearby` is the
straight line between Google's coordinates, not a travel distance.

A location in `routes.*` is exactly one of `address`, `place_id` (from a
search) or `lat` and `lng`. `mode` is `drive` (the default), `walk`,
`bicycle` or `transit`. `departure_time` is ISO 8601 with an offset;
the agent does not guess a time zone. Driving with a departure time
asks Google for traffic: `duration_in_traffic_minutes` is the estimate
with traffic, `duration_minutes` the same trip without it. Every routes
answer carries `estimated_at`, the moment it was asked.

No records: saved places ("the office") are left to the conversation
for now; a small record type would earn its place once people ask for
the same origin every day.

## Setup

1. In a Google Cloud project of the organization's, with billing
   enabled, enable **Places API (New)** and **Routes API** (APIs &
   Services → Library). The older "Places API" and "Distance Matrix
   API" are different products; this agent uses neither.
2. Create an API key (APIs & Services → Credentials → Create
   credentials → API key).
3. Restrict it: under **API restrictions** choose "Restrict key" and
   select only Places API (New) and Routes API. The key is called from
   the platform's servers, so an application restriction by IP address
   is the right one if the deployment's egress address is fixed.
4. Paste the key into the agent's Credentials tab as **Google Maps
   Platform key**, grant it to this agent, and ask the assistant to
   check the key — `account_status` names any API still switched off.

`api_base_url` is for tests only; leave it empty.

## Billing, honestly

**These APIs are billed per request, to the Google Cloud project the
key belongs to — the organization's, not the person asking.** Google
bills each call by the most expensive field its field mask names, so
every call here names only the fields it reads (never `*`). As Google
documents its SKUs at the time of writing — check Google's pricing
page, which changes:

| Call | Fields asked | SKU tier it falls in |
|---|---|---|
| `account_status` | Text Search `places.id`; a route request with no destination, which Google refuses before routing | Text Search Essentials (IDs Only), free; a refused request is not billed |
| `places_search` | id, name, address, location, Maps link | Text Search Pro; **Enterprise** when `include` names rating, price, open now, hours, phone or website |
| `places_nearby` | the same row fields | Nearby Search Pro (Enterprise with `include`); a `place_id` centre adds one Place Details Essentials call (`location` only) |
| `places_details` | the row fields plus business status | Place Details Pro (Enterprise with `include`) |
| `routes_distance` | distance, duration, static duration, condition | Route Matrix Essentials per destination; **Pro** when driving with a departure time (traffic) |
| `routes_between` | distance, durations, description, warnings, steps; for transit also `transitDetails` and the fare | Compute Routes Essentials; **Pro** with traffic, or for transit details |

Google's monthly free usage per SKU applies first. The agent's
instructions tell the assistant not to repeat a search whose answer it
already has, but nothing here caps spend: set quotas on the APIs in the
Cloud console if the organization wants a ceiling.

## Errors

| `kind` | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `auth` | The key is invalid, an API is not enabled (named), the key's restrictions block an API (named), or billing is off — a person fixes the setup |
| `not_found` | Google has no place with that id |
| `invalid` | Google refused what was asked (its words say why), or an input was refused before Google was asked |
| `rate` | Google answered 429 `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED` (a per-minute quota, or one the organization set) or 503, and it lasted past a short wait |
| `http` | Anything else, or Google could not be reached after several tries |

A missing credential is a plain answer from `account_status`
(`connected: false`) and `kind: auth` from everything else.

## Limits, and what is not verified

- Live Google Maps Platform behaviour is **not yet verified**: the tests
  run the agent's program against a loopback stub
  (`tests/maps_stub.py`) that refuses, as Google does, a request without
  a key or a field mask, a mask path Google does not know, a bare field
  without its `places.`/`routes.` prefix, and a traffic preference on a
  mode other than driving; it returns only the fields a mask names. The
  field names follow Google's REST reference; they have not been
  exercised against the real APIs.
- Every request runs off the agent's loop on the shared client; a busy
  API is waited out (honouring `Retry-After`) within 20 seconds.
- Results are capped at 20 places and 20 destinations per call, text
  fields clipped.
- One origin per `routes_distance` call; no waypoints, no alternative
  routes, no tolls or fuel options.
- A past `departure_time` is refused for everything but transit, which
  Google plans from 7 days back to 100 days ahead.
- Directions links are built from the inputs in Google Maps URL form;
  the link opens Google Maps, which plans the route afresh.

agent.name: Spreadsheets
agent.description: Reads the CSV, Excel and JSON files you upload and tells you what is in them and what is wrong with them: duplicates, gaps, numbers that can't be read without a guess. Reconciles two lists by rules you state, totals and pivots in code, sorts and filters into a new file, checks JSON against a schema and turns JSON into a table and back. No number is added up by a model.
agent.instructions:
Use this agent when the user attached a CSV, Excel (.xlsx), JSON or JSON Lines file, or wants one produced. Start with read_inspect (or json_inspect for JSON): it gives the sheets, the header row it found (titles above it are skipped), the row count, each column's type and its decimal mark. Read data with read_rows; it is paged, continue with next_row. All arithmetic, matching, sorting and filtering is done here in code: never add up, compare or match rows yourself, and never retype numbers from memory.
Numbers are read the way each column writes them: 1.234,56 and 12,50 use a decimal comma, 1,234.56 a decimal point. A column holding only values like 1,234 or 2.500 is ambiguous: the agent refuses it and names the values. Ask the person whether 1,234 means one thousand two hundred and thirty-four or 1.234, then pass decimal "." or ",". Never choose for them. A column of two currencies is never totalled. Identifiers (leading zero, a leading +, more than 15 digits) stay text.
A file is read whole or refused with its row count; nothing is cut silently. When a header isn't found, pass header_row (the sheet's own row number). Formulas are carried into new files as the values the file computed, each with a note giving the formula; say so when formulas_as_values is above zero.
check_quality finds duplicates, blank required cells and spelling variants. reconcile_match compares two lists by the key columns the person names; rows equal on all keys but one are uncertain and never merged; a blank key matches nothing. clean_dedupe, clean_convert (numbers stored as text made numbers), combine_files (one workbook from several files, with totals), arrange_rows (filter and sort into a new xlsx or csv), calc_aggregate and calc_pivot (sums by group, and group by column) all compute in code. Produced files are read back first; give the user the file_ref and report what the change log and the not-converted list say. CSVs are written in UTF-8 with a byte-order mark so Excel shows Arabic.
JSON: json_select reads values by path (a.b, a[0], a[*], *, $). json_validate checks a JSON Schema, formats included (email, date, date-time, uri); report its errors with their paths, and never call a file valid unless it says so. json_compare is exact: 1 and true differ, "1" and 1 differ. json_filter keeps records by conditions; json_to_table and json_from_table cross to CSV and back. A JSON Lines line that doesn't parse is named by its line number.
Ask before treating an uncertain match as the same record, and before choosing a decimal mark.

functions.name: Inspect Spreadsheet
functions.description: The sheets of a CSV or Excel file (name, rows of data, the header row found, merged ranges) and one entry per column: its type (text, number, date, mixed, empty), blanks, formulas, identifiers with leading zeros, its decimal mark ("." or ",", or "ambiguous"/"mixed" with examples) and the currencies written in it. A CSV's encoding and delimiter are found and said. A file past 100,000 rows is refused with its count, never cut.

functions.name: Read Rows
functions.description: Rows of one sheet as objects keyed by column name, from from_row (1 = the first row under the header), up to max_rows; next_row says where to continue, and first_sheet_row is the sheet's own row number. Values come as text as they appear, so identifiers keep their zeros; with formulas=true a formula cell shows its formula.

functions.name: Check Quality
functions.description: Duplicates by key_columns (trimmed, case ignored, digits only for phone columns; a row with a blank key is counted, never a duplicate), rows with blank required_columns, and values in categorical_columns that differ only by case or spacing. Row numbers are the sheet's own. Recorded as a job.

functions.name: Reconcile Two Lists
functions.description: Rows of A against rows of B by keys — each key names a column in A, the column in B, and how both are normalized (trim, lowercase, digits, none). Equal on every key: matched. Equal on all but one key: uncertain, shown side by side, never merged. A key with a blank part matches nothing. compare names columns to diff on matched rows. Looked up by hash, so large lists take seconds. Writes a workbook with sheets Matched, Only in A, Only in B, Uncertain, Differences and Change Log, read back before it is returned.

functions.name: Remove Duplicates
functions.description: A new workbook: sheet Clean keeps the first row of every group equal on key_columns (after normalization), sheet Removed lists the rest with their original row numbers, sheet Change Log says what was done. A row with a blank key is kept and never called a duplicate. Identifiers and dates are kept as they were; formulas become the values the file computed, each with a note giving the formula. The original file is untouched.

functions.name: Make Numbers Numbers
functions.description: A new workbook where the named columns' numbers stored as text ("1.234,56", "AED 1,250.00", "٣٤٥٫٥") become real numbers, each read with its column's own decimal mark. A column whose mark can't be told is refused until decimal is given. A cell that isn't a number — or is an identifier such as 00412 or +9715… — is left as it was and listed with why. The original file is untouched.

functions.name: Combine Into Workbook
functions.description: A new workbook from several CSV or Excel files: sheet Summary has one line per file (rows, the total of total_column, values that are not numbers, and any problem — a file that could not be read, columns missing or extra against the first file, a column whose decimal mark can't be told), sheet All holds every row with a Source column, then one sheet per file, then the Change Log. Each file's numbers are read with its own decimal mark and totalled in code.

functions.name: Aggregate
functions.description: Rows grouped by group_by and measured (sum, count, avg, min, max) in exact decimals, each column read with its own decimal mark. A cell that is not a number is skipped and counted, with examples; a column whose mark can't be told is refused until decimal is given. At most 500 groups: more is refused with the count. Recorded as a job.

functions.name: Pivot Table
functions.description: A pivot computed in code: rows grouped by one or two columns (rows), against the values of across, each crossing the sum (or count) of values, with a total for every row and column and a grand total. At most 300 rows by 40 columns, refused past that with the count. With filename, also written as a workbook.

functions.name: Filter and Sort Into a File
functions.description: The rows that meet the filters (all or any), in the order sort gives, with the chosen columns, into a new xlsx or csv file. Numbers compare as numbers read with their column's decimal mark, dates (YYYY-MM-DD) as dates, the rest as text ignoring case; blanks sort last. A CSV is UTF-8 with a byte-order mark.

functions.name: Inspect JSON
functions.description: Whether a file is valid JSON or JSON Lines (a line that doesn't parse is named by its number, and nothing is half-read), its top-level type, how many records, and the key map: every path the records use, how many have it, the types seen and one example, from the first max_records.

functions.name: Values by Path
functions.description: The values at a path, each with the exact path it was found at: a.b for a nested key, a[0] for one item (a[-1] the last), a[*] for every item, * for every value, $ for the whole document. A large value is cut and marked.

functions.name: Check Against a Schema
functions.description: The file against a JSON Schema, given inline (schema) or as an attached file (schema_ref). Formats are checked: email, date, date-time, time, uri, ipv4, ipv6, uuid. With record_path (or each_record) every record is checked on its own, and failures carry the record's index, the path, the rule and the message. A schema that is itself invalid is refused as the schema's fault. Recorded as a job.

functions.name: Compare Two JSON Files
functions.description: What changed between two JSON files, path by path: added, removed, changed, with before and after as JSON text, and the type when it changed. Exact: 1 and true differ, "1" and 1 differ, 1 and 1.0 are equal. Arrays compare by position.

functions.name: Filter JSON Records
functions.description: The records (those at record_path, or the file's own) that meet the conditions, all or any, into a new JSON file. Each condition is a path inside the record, an op and a value: eq and ne compare exactly (1 is not true), gt/gte/lt/lte compare numbers with numbers and text with text (an ISO date compares as text), contains looks in text or a list, exists and missing need no value.

functions.name: JSON to CSV
functions.description: A CSV from the records (those at record_path, or the file's own), nested values as dotted columns (customer.city), a list as its JSON text; columns picks and orders them. UTF-8 with a byte-order mark, so Excel shows Arabic; read back before it is returned.

functions.name: CSV or Excel to JSON
functions.description: A JSON file from a CSV or a sheet, one object per row; dotted column names (customer.city) become nested objects. With infer_types, numbers become numbers when their column's writing says so and nothing is lost; identifiers (007, +9715…, sixteen digits), amounts with a currency and columns whose decimal mark can't be told stay text; true, false and null become themselves. NaN and infinity are never written.

agents.readme:
# Spreadsheets (`sheets`)

A branch sends its monthly sales as a CSV saved by Arabic Windows Excel: two title lines above the header,
semicolons between the fields, and amounts written `12.450,50`. Ask for the totals by branch and month and the
answer is computed here, in code, with every amount read the way its column writes it — not a hundred times too
large, and not guessed when the column doesn't say.

Reads CSV, Excel (`.xlsx`), JSON and JSON Lines files; finds duplicates, gaps and spelling variants; reconciles two
lists by the rules you state; totals, pivots, filters and sorts into new files; checks JSON against a schema; and
turns JSON into a table and back. Version 2.0.0 absorbs the JSON agent (`json_data`).

No external service and no credential. Files come in as platform files — a person's upload in the chat, or a file
another agent saved — by `file_ref`. Produced files go back as the call's files; the original is never modified.

## Supported formats

| Kind | Read | Produced |
|---|---|---|
| CSV, TSV | yes: encoding found (UTF-8 with or without its mark, UTF-16, cp1256 for Arabic, cp1252), delimiter found (`,` `;` tab `\|`) | yes: UTF-8 with a byte-order mark, so Excel shows Arabic |
| Excel `.xlsx` | yes: every sheet, merged cells, formulas with their computed values | yes |
| JSON, JSON Lines | yes | yes (`json_filter`, `json_from_table`) |
| Legacy `.xls`, `.ods`, Numbers | no — reported as unsupported | — |

## Functions

| Function | Level | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `read_inspect` | 0 | Sheets, the header row found, rows, merged ranges; per column its type, blanks, formulas, leading zeros, decimal mark and currencies; a CSV's encoding and delimiter |
| `read_rows` | 0 | Rows as text, paged (`from_row`, `next_row`); `formulas=true` shows formulas |
| `check_quality` | 1 | Duplicates by key, blank required cells, spelling variants. Recorded |
| `reconcile_match` | 1 | Two lists matched by key rules; near matches uncertain, never merged; a workbook with a change log |
| `clean_dedupe` | 1 | A workbook without duplicates, the removed rows listed |
| `clean_convert` | 1 | Numbers stored as text made numbers ("prices as numbers"); what wasn't converted listed with why |
| `combine_files` | 1 | Several files into one workbook with a summary and totals |
| `calc_aggregate` | 1 | Sum, count, avg, min, max by group; at most 500 groups |
| `calc_pivot` | 1 | Group × column sums (or counts) with row, column and grand totals; optionally a workbook |
| `arrange_rows` | 1 | Filter and sort into a new xlsx or csv |
| `json_inspect` | 0 | Valid or not, JSON or JSON Lines, records, and the key map |
| `json_select` | 0 | Values at a path |
| `json_validate` | 1 | A JSON Schema check, formats included, per record. Recorded |
| `json_compare` | 0 | What changed, path by path |
| `json_filter` | 1 | Records kept by conditions, into a JSON file |
| `json_to_table` | 1 | JSON to CSV, nested keys as dotted columns |
| `json_from_table` | 1 | CSV or a sheet to JSON, dotted columns nested again |

A function that produces a file also writes a `job` record (what it read, what it wrote, its summary), so it is
level 1; nothing here acts outside the platform. None is schedulable: each works on a file someone hands it.

## Numbers, the way the column writes them

- **The decimal mark is read per column.** `1.234,56` and `12,50` say a decimal comma; `1,234.56` and `12.50` a
  decimal point; the Arabic decimal mark `٫` and thousands mark `٬` say themselves; Arabic-Indic digits are digits.
- **An ambiguous column is refused, not guessed.** A column of nothing but `1,250` and `2,500` could be thousands or
  decimals: the agent names the values and asks for `decimal` (`.` or `,`). A column writing both marks is refused
  the same way.
- **A currency beside an amount** (`AED 1,250.00`, `1.250,00 د.إ`) is noted; a column of two currencies is never
  totalled. `json_from_table` keeps such an amount as text.
- **Identifiers stay text:** a leading zero (`00412`), a leading `+` (`+971501234567`), or more than fifteen digits.
- All arithmetic is in exact decimals.

## Honest about the file

- **Nothing is cut silently.** A sheet past 100,000 rows of data, or a file past 1,500,000 cells, is refused with its
  count. A file larger than a chat file may be (8 MiB less 64 KiB) is refused with its size before it is read.
- **The header is found** under titles, a report date or blank rows, or named with `header_row`; row numbers are the
  sheet's own.
- **Merged cells** carry their value over the whole range, so a merged region label is not read as blanks.
- **Formulas are never moved as broken text.** A formula copied to another sheet or file points at other cells, so a
  produced workbook holds the value the source computed, with a note on the cell giving the formula and where it
  stood; a formula the file never computed is left empty and said. A text cell that starts with `=` is told apart
  from a formula by its type, and stays text.
- **A blank key matches nothing**, in duplicates and in reconciliation: two rows with no email are not one person.
- **Reconciliation is by hash**, near-linear: two lists of tens of thousands of rows take seconds.
- **JSON is JSON:** `1` is not `true`, `"1"` is not `1`, `NaN` and `Infinity` are refused where they stand and never
  written; a JSON Lines line that doesn't parse is named by its number.
- Parsing and writing run off the agent's loop, so one large file doesn't stall the chat's other calls.
- A produced sheet whose words are mostly Arabic is set right to left.

## The JSON path language

`$` the whole document; `a.b` a nested key; `a[0]` one item (`a[-1]` the last); `a[*]` every item; `*` every value of
an object. There is no arithmetic in a path; `json_filter` conditions compare in code.

## Sample data

Sidra Office Supplies (fictional): a supplier price list with a duplicated row, a missing price and a price that is
not a number, and the product catalog to reconcile it with; an Arabic branch sales report as Gulf Excel saves it
(titles above the header, semicolons, a decimal comma); and an order export with gaps and the schema it should meet.
All in `samples/` (`samples.yaml`).

## Limits, and what is not verified

- `.xlsx` only; `.xls` and `.ods` are refused as unsupported.
- A formula's value is the one the file last computed; the agent doesn't recalculate.
- Delimiter and single-byte encoding are inferred from the text (cp1256 when Arabic words dominate, else cp1252);

- Produced workbooks are verified by reading them back with the library that wrote them; rendered appearance is not
  inspected.
- The tests run the agent as its own program, against fixtures written out in full in the test file.

agents.readme:
# Slack (`slack`)

"What was said in #showroom this morning?" — read as text, oldest first, with names instead of user ids. "Has anyone
answered my question about the chairs?" — answered from the thread and the conversation after it. "Send Dana a
message that the samples arrived" — Dana found by name or address, the text shown to you word for word, sent as you
only when you say so. "Open the spreadsheet Omar shared" — brought into the chat. And "tell me whenever someone
mentions me or messages me" — a watch that a schedule checks, waking the assistant only when something arrived.

One person's Slack over the Slack Web API, signed in with a **user token**: the agent sees what that person sees,
and what it sends is sent in their name. Several workspaces may be connected; every function takes `account`.

## Functions

| Function | Level | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `account_status` | 0 | The connection: workspace, user name and user id, for each account |
| `conversations_list` | 0 | Channels, private channels, group DMs and DMs the person is in; DMs named by the other person |
| `conversations_messages` | 0 | Recent messages, oldest first, with authors, reply counts, shared files and links; `oldest` alone gives the first ones after it |
| `conversations_replies` | 0 | A thread's parent and replies, oldest first |
| `messages_search` | 0 | Slack search (`in:#channel`, `from:@name`, `after:`, `on:`), newest first |
| `messages_answered` | 0 | Whether anyone other than the person wrote after a message, in its thread or the conversation, and who |
| `people_find` | 0 | Someone by address (`users.lookupByEmail`), full name, part of a name, `@handle` or user id; several matches come back as candidates |
| `files_read` | 0 | A file shared in a conversation, brought into the chat (at most 8 MiB less 64 KiB) |
| `messages_send` | 3 | Text posted as the person to a conversation, optionally into a thread |
| `messages_direct` | 3 | A direct message to one person by address, name or user id; the conversation is opened (`conversations.open`) if it never was |
| `reactions_add`, `reactions_remove` | 3 | An emoji reaction as the person, or taken back |
| `watch_start` | 1 | Start watching mentions, DMs, or both, from now; conversations can be left out |
| `watch_new` | 1, schedulable | What arrived since the last check, oldest first, each row a mention or a dm |
| `watches_list` | 0 | The open watches (closed ones too, when asked) |
| `watches_close` | 1 | Stop a watch for good |

Records: `sent` — every message this agent posted, where, and the `ts` Slack gave it (its text kept encrypted, in
`values`). `watch` — what is watched, on which account, and each source's place.

## Rules it keeps

- **Nothing is said without a yes.** Sending, direct messages and reactions are level 3: others see them.
- **Nothing is said twice.** A send that gets no answer is of unknown outcome and not retried; a send Slack refused
  with 429 (so did nothing) is sent again after the wait it named.
- **Nothing is guessed.** Conversation ids, user ids and `ts` values are Slack's own, passed on unchanged. A name
  two people share is never picked between: the candidates come back so the person chooses.
- **Answers stay small.** At most 25 messages per answer, long text clipped, `more` says when there is more.
- **Failures have kinds:** `auth` (reconnect), `scope` (the account was connected without a permission this needs,
  such as `files:read` for an account connected through 1.0.0: reconnect it), `not_found`, `denied`, `rate` (Slack's
  `Retry-After` waited out when short, reported when long), `invalid`, `too_large`, `http`, `unknown`.

## Watching mentions and DMs

Record a watch once with `watch_start`, then schedule `watch_new` every few minutes. Each check, with no model, reads
each watch on its own: one that fails keeps its place and is named in `problems`; the others are handed on.

- **Mentions** come from Slack search (`<@USERID>`), whose index lags. Each check looks 15 minutes behind the newest
  mention it handed on and leaves out the ones it already handed on, so a mention indexed late still comes, once.
- **DMs and group DMs** each keep their own place. Every one is read in turn: those Slack marks as updated first, then
  the least recently read. History pages run newest first; when one read cannot reach back to a conversation's
  place, the next read narrows to below what it saw, so a burst is handed on whole, oldest first, never stepped over.
- The person's own messages and skipped conversations are left out; a mention inside a DM is one `dm` row.

## Slack's rate limits (2025)

Since 29 May 2025 (existing installations from 3 March 2026), an app **distributed to other workspaces outside the
Slack Marketplace** may call `conversations.history` and `conversations.replies` once a minute, 15 messages a page.
An organization's **own app, installed only in its own workspace**, keeps 50+ a minute and up to 999 a page. Register
the Slack app per deployment, in the workspace it serves, to keep the second.

Under the first, the agent still works, more slowly: reading a conversation asks for one page; a long thread or a
`messages_answered` that needs two reads may come back as `rate`; and the watch reads one conversation a minute,
stopping its DMs at the first 429 with every place kept and `more` set, while mentions (search, not limited) are
handed on as usual.

## Setup

1. At <https://api.slack.com/apps>, **Create New App** → *From scratch*, in the workspace it will be used with.
2. Under **OAuth & Permissions**, add the redirect URL the platform shows on **Settings → Connected apps** for
   provider `slack`. Slack takes only an https redirect URL.
3. Under **User Token Scopes** (not Bot Token Scopes) add: `channels:read`, `channels:history`, `groups:read`,
   `groups:history`, `im:read`, `im:history`, `im:write`, `mpim:read`, `mpim:history`, `users:read`,
   `users:read.email`, `search:read`, `chat:write`, `reactions:write`, `files:read`.
4. Leave **token rotation** off. The platform then holds a long-lived user token; this agent never refreshes one.
5. From **Basic Information**, copy the Client ID and Client Secret and register them under **Settings → Connected
   apps** as provider `slack`.
6. Install the agent, open its Credentials tab and connect. Every person connects their own account. An account
   connected through 1.0.0 lacks `im:write`, `reactions:write` and `files:read`: reconnect it to use those.

`api_base_url` on the credential exists for the tests' loopback Slack; leave it empty.

## What it will not do

- No edits, deletes, file uploads, scheduled messages or group DMs opened by the agent.
- Files larger than 8 MiB less 64 KiB are refused before download, with their Slack link; files kept outside Slack
  (Google Drive and the like) are refused with their link, and the token is never sent there.
- The watch reads DM history, which holds top-level messages, not thread replies; a reply in a DM thread is seen only
  if it mentions the person.
- More than 300 mentions between two checks: the oldest beyond three search pages may be missed.
- Tested only against a loopback stub of the Web API subset it uses; the first real connection is the first live run.

agent.description: Everything you have to do, and everything that renews or expires, in one list. Paste meeting notes and get the action items to confirm; record a subscription, a lease or a passport and be told before the day you must act — the notice deadline, not the renewal date. Ask what is overdue, what is coming up, and what was done.
agent.instructions: Use this agent for anything someone has to do by a date, and for anything that renews or expires. Tasks: record one with tasks_create, never inventing an owner or a date; a task may repeat daily, weekly, monthly or yearly (it needs a due date), and completing it makes the next one by itself. Priority is high, normal or low. Mark a task done only with what shows it was done (a message id, a file, a reference) in evidence. Pass the person's timezone (IANA, such as Asia/Dubai) to every function that takes one, so "today" is their day, not UTC's. From meeting notes, pass the text to extract_propose with the meeting date; show the proposals: each quotes the passage it came from, is marked commitment or suggestion, and says verified false when its quote is not in the notes word for word. Read every date_readings line to the person: a weekday or a date without a year was read, not stated, and "next Friday" is left for them to resolve. Confirm only what they agree to (extract_confirm); an unverified proposal is refused unless the person has seen its quote and you pass accept_unverified. Confirming twice is safe: the second finds the task. Renewals: from a document, pass its text (the Documents agent's text) to agreements_extract, which proposes the dates and terms with each clause quoted and checked, and names what is ambiguous or missing; ask the person for every exact date, basis or currency the text does not give, and never guess one. Amounts are text with a decimal point ("4800.50"), and the currency is the three-letter code the person or document gives: never assume one. Then agreements_create records it and derives two deadlines: the renewal date, and the notice deadline (the renewal date minus the notice period, in calendar or business days; business days follow work_week, mon_fri by default or sun_thu). A reminder, a completed deadline or a recorded decision is not a cancellation or a renewal: agreements_set_status changes the state only with the confirmation's reference. For "what needs me", use tasks_overdue and deadlines_upcoming; both are deterministic, and either can run on a schedule. A reading of a document is not legal advice; say so when it matters.

agents.readme:
# Tasks (`tasks`)

A meeting ends with six promises and no list. The office lease renews for
another three years unless someone gives notice ninety days before. Both
are the same question — what must I do, and by when — and this agent
keeps both.

Paste the notes: the assistant reads out the action items with the
passage that states each, you confirm them, and they become tasks with
owners and dates. Record a subscription, a lease, an insurance policy or
a passport once, with the clause it came from, and ask each month what
falls due: the answer names the day you must act — the notice deadline,
not the renewal date — and whose decision it is.

No external service. The model is used only to read notes and documents;
every quote it returns is checked verbatim against the text. All date
arithmetic is code.

## Functions

**Tasks** — obligations, and the action items read out of notes.

| Function | Level | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `tasks_create` | 1 | A task, with owner and due only as given; a priority; repeating daily, weekly or monthly |
| `tasks_update` | 1 | Status, owner, due, note, priority, repeat; done needs evidence, blocked needs a blocker; done on a repeating task makes the next one |
| `tasks_list` | 0 | By owner, status, source, priority; due date first, then priority |
| `tasks_overdue` | 0, schedulable | As of a date (today in the person's zone): overdue, due soon, blocked, unassigned, undated |
| `extract_propose` | 1, uses the chat's model | Proposals from notes with verified quotes, commitment or suggestion, owner and date only when the notes give them, and each date reading said |
| `extract_confirm` | 1 | Proposals the user agreed to become tasks; owner and due may be supplied now; unverified ones only when accepted; safe to repeat |
| `extract_reject` | 1 | A proposal marked not wanted |

**Renewals** — anything that renews or expires: a subscription, a
contract, an insurance policy, a warranty, a maintenance plan, a lease,
a licence, a passport or visa.

| Function | Level | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `agreements_extract` | 0, uses the chat's model | Reads a document's text; proposes the counterparty, dates, term, notice period and auto-renewal with verbatim clauses; names ambiguities and asks; records nothing |
| `agreements_create` | 1 | Records it with its clauses; derives the renewal and notice deadlines; says what is still to ask |
| `agreements_get` | 0 | One renewal with its clauses, deadlines and decisions |
| `agreements_update` | 1 | Changes dates, notice period or basis, owner, auto-renewal, value, note; recomputes and moves the open deadlines |
| `agreements_set_status` | 1 | Renewed or cancelled (each needs evidence and a name; renewed also the new renewal date), or expired |
| `deadlines_upcoming` | 0, schedulable | What is due or passed within a window, what awaits a decision, what cannot be computed |
| `deadlines_add` | 1 | A further deadline: warranty end, expiry, review, custom |
| `deadlines_complete` | 1 | Records a deadline acted on, with evidence; never cancels anything |
| `decisions_record` | 1 | The intended decision (renew, cancel, renegotiate), by whom and when |

Records: `task` and `agreement` (both editable on the page), `extraction`
(proposals, with what became of each), `clause`, `deadline`, `decision`.

## Proposals are not tasks

`extract_propose` asks the chat's model for the action items and, for
each, the exact passage that states it. Then the code checks:

- the quote must appear verbatim in the notes, or the proposal is marked
  `verified: false`;
- the owner must be a whole name the notes (or the `people` list)
  actually contain, or it is cleared — an owner is never invented, and
  "Al" is not "Alice";
- the due date is accepted when the notes state it whole (ISO, or a
  day, month and year), or read from `meeting_date` (a weekday name, a
  day and month without a year); a read date comes with `due_reading`,
  the sentence that says what it was read as, and the call lists them
  all in `date_readings`. "Next Friday" and "next week" stay as
  `due_text` for a person to decide.

`verified` is kept on the proposal. `extract_confirm` refuses an
unverified one unless the person has seen its quote and the call says
`accept_unverified`. Confirming is safe to repeat: the proposal is
marked before its task is made and the task names its proposal, so a
retry after a lost answer hands back the same task, never a second.

## Recurring tasks and priority

A task may repeat `daily`, `weekly` or `monthly`; it needs a due date to
count from. Marking it done makes the next one, once (a second "done"
finds it): due one step after the previous due date, or the first step
after the day it was done when it was done late. A monthly task keeps
its day of the month: the 31st becomes the 28th in February and the
31st again in March. Priority is `high`, `normal` (the default) or
`low`, and orders tasks due the same day.

A commitment is something a named person said they will do; a suggestion
is something someone said should be done. Both are proposals until
`extract_confirm`, where the user can add the owner or date the notes
lacked. A task confirmed without an owner is listed as unassigned until
someone takes it.

## Two dates, not one

Something that renews on 1 December with 60 days' notice has a renewal
deadline on 1 December and a notice deadline on 2 October (calendar
days) or 8 September (business days, Monday to Friday). The agent
computes the notice deadline only when it has all three: the exact
renewal date, the notice period in days, and the basis. While any is
missing it records what it has and returns `asks` naming what to get
from the user or the document. It never picks a basis, never completes
"December" into a day, and never turns "two months" into a number of
days.

`agreements_extract` asks the model for the dates and terms as written
and the clauses they come from. Code then checks each quote against the
text (`verified`), parses each date (only an exact day, month and year
counts), reads the notice period ("60 days", "60 business days", "sixty
(60) calendar days") and marks a clause `ambiguous` when the notice
period has no basis or the renewal date has no day. Nothing is recorded
until `agreements_create`.

## What needs me

Two deterministic checks, both fit for a schedule. Neither asks a model.

- `tasks_overdue`: what is late, what is due
  within `within_days`, what is blocked, and what has no owner or no date.
- `deadlines_upcoming`: every open deadline inside
  the window or already passed, with calendar and business days left;
  `awaiting_decision` for renewals whose notice deadline is near with no
  decision recorded; `incomplete` for those whose deadline could not be
  computed, and why.

## What is and is not a cancellation

- A reminder is a reminder.
- `deadlines_complete` on the notice deadline records that notice was
  given, with the message reference; the renewal stays active.
- `decisions_record` records an intention.
- Only `agreements_set_status` with the confirmation reference and a name
  marks something renewed or cancelled. Renewed takes the new renewal
  date and derives the next notice deadline.

## Sample data

What Sidra Office Supplies' last two meetings left to do: five tasks
(one blocked, one done, one with no owner) and two proposals waiting
to be confirmed. Three renewals with their clauses and deadlines: an office
lease whose notice deadline is 1 December 2026, an accounting
subscription whose notice deadline is 16 October 2026, and a printer
maintenance contract whose notice was due by 2 August 2026.

## Limits

- Dates are calendar dates; there are no times of day. "Today" is the
  person's when the call is given their `timezone`, and UTC otherwise.
- Business days follow the renewal's `work_week`: Monday to Friday by
  default, or Sunday to Thursday; public holidays are not known.
- Notice periods in months are reported as ambiguous, not converted.
- Extraction quality depends on the chat's model; the checks catch a
  misquote, an invented name and an ambiguous date, not a missed item.
- Documents are read from supplied text (use the Documents agent for PDF
  and Word); scanned pages without a text layer cannot be read.
- Values are exact decimals kept as text ("4800.50"), with the currency
  the person or document gave; none is assumed, and nothing is converted
  between currencies.

agents.readme:
# Microsoft Teams (`teams`)

"What did I miss?" answered from your unread chats, counted in code. "What did Dana say?" read as text, oldest
first. "Tell her the drawings are coming Thursday" shown to you word for word and sent only when you say so. "Has she
replied?" answered from the chat itself. A watch on a schedule hands on each new chat message once.

A work or school (Microsoft 365) account's Teams over Microsoft Graph. A personal Microsoft account has no Teams API:
every function says so before anything is asked of Microsoft. It rides the same Microsoft connection as every other
Microsoft agent; several accounts may be connected, and every function takes `account`.

## Functions

| Function | Level | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `account_status` | 0 | The connection, whose account it is, and whether it can use Teams |
| `chats_list` | 0 | Chats by their latest message, newest first (Graph's own order), paged; `with` narrows by a person |
| `chats_read` | 0 | A chat's messages as text, oldest first, up to 200 at once, paged further back |
| `chats_missed` | 0 | Unread (or recent) chats with what others said since a time |
| `chats_send` | 3 | Text to a chat, or to a person by address (their one-to-one chat, found or started), with @mentions |
| `chats_replies` | 0 | Whether anyone answered something this agent sent, read back past 50 messages |
| `teams_list`, `channels_list` | 0 | Teams, and a team's channels |
| `channels_read`, `channels_replies` | 0 | A channel's posts and a post's replies (needs an administrator's consent, below) |
| `channels_post`, `channels_reply` | 3 | A post (with subject and @mentions), or a reply in a post's thread |
| `watches_start` | 1 | Watch one chat, or every chat, for new messages from others |
| `watches_check` | 1 | Schedulable: each new message since the last check, once |
| `watches_list`, `watches_close` | 0, 1 | The watches, and stopping one for good |

Records: `sent` (every attempt, where it went, and what became of it; the words and recipients encrypted) and
`watch`.

## Rules it keeps

- **Nothing is said without a yes,** and nothing twice. A send is one request to Microsoft. It is recorded as
  `sending` before it goes and `sent`, `unknown` or `failed` after. No answer means `unknown`: never retried. The same
  words to the same place after an unknown attempt are looked for in the chat first; if they are not there, they go
  only when the person says to send them again.
- **Times fit the call.** Each request has its own timeout and Microsoft's "busy, wait" (429) is waited out within a
  cap, so a function answers before the platform's clock runs out.
- **Text in, text out.** Teams returns HTML; it is read as text. Plain messages go as text; a message with mentions
  goes as HTML, escaped.

## Channel messages and the administrator

The shared Microsoft sign-in asks only for permissions a person can grant themselves. Reading channel messages needs
`ChannelMessage.Read.All`, which only an administrator can consent to, so `channels_read` and `channels_replies`
are refused with that explanation unless an organization adds it. Posting and replying in channels work without it.
Mentions in a channel find the person's Teams id among the members of the account's chats, since listing a team's
members needs another administrator permission.

## Limits

- No attachments, reactions or edits; no search across all of Teams.
- `chats_missed` reads up to 250 chats and 25 of them in detail; `chats_replies` reads back 500 messages.
- Verified against a loopback stub held to Microsoft's documented query rules; see the first-live-run list in the
  release notes.

agents.readme:
# Timesheets (`timesheets`)

Friday afternoon, and the week has to be accounted for. Ask for this
week's meetings to become timesheet entries: the showroom meetings
with Harbourline land on the showroom project, the stand-ups on admin,
and the lunch no rule knows about comes back as a question rather than
a guess. Then ask where the gaps are — Wednesday, two hours — fill it,
submit the week, and get the workbook to send.

## Functions

| Function | Level | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `projects_add` | 1 | A project, by short code; billable unless said otherwise, with an optional hour budget |
| `projects_list` | 0 | Projects with hours logged and budget left |
| `projects_update` | 1 | Rename, change the client, billable or budget, archive |
| `projects_add_rule` | 1 | Place meetings on a project when the title, an attendee or the location contains a text |
| `projects_rules` | 0 | The rules |
| `projects_remove_rule` | 2 | Deletes a rule; what it placed stays |
| `entries_log` | 1 | Hours on a project on a day (today in the person's zone by default) — a number, or a start and end |
| `entries_from_events` | 1 | Calendar meetings into entries, by the rules; returns what it could not place |
| `entries_list` | 0 | A week's entries, or a date range's, with the total |
| `entries_update` | 1 | Changes an entry in an open week |
| `entries_remove` | 2 | Deletes an entry from an open week |
| `weeks_summary` | 0 | The week by project and day, billable hours, and the gaps |
| `weeks_gaps` | 0, schedulable | This week's short working days up to yesterday, and a sentence that says so; no model |
| `weeks_submit` | 1 | Hands the week in; its entries lock |
| `weeks_reopen` | 1 | Unlocks a submitted week |
| `weeks_workbook` | 0 | The week as an Excel workbook, read back cell by cell before it is handed back as the call's file |
| `timer_start` | 1 | Starts timing work on a project; one timer at a time |
| `timer_stop` | 1 | Stops it and logs the time, to the quarter hour, on the day it started; over 10 hours it asks first |
| `timer_status` | 0 | What is running, since when |
| `timer_cancel` | 1 | Stops it without logging |

Records: `project`, `rule`, `entry` (hours on one project on one day),
`week` (a week handed in, and when) and `timer` (time running on a
project).

## From the calendar, by your rules

The calendar agents list meetings; this agent takes those rows as they
are. Each meeting's length is rounded to the quarter hour and logged
on the day it took place. Which project it goes on is decided by the
user's rules, in plain terms — the title contains "Harbourline", an
attendee's address contains "harbourline.example", the location
contains "Riverside". A meeting no rule places, or one that two rules
place on different projects (the "Harbourline stand-up"), comes back
unassigned with the reason; the user's answers go back in as
`assign`, an event id and a project code for each. A meeting already
on the timesheet is not logged again, an all-day, cancelled or
declined one is not time spent, and one in a submitted week is
skipped.

## Rules it keeps

- **Nothing guesses a project.**
- **A day holds at most 24 hours.**
- **Today is the person's.** Every function that defaults to today or
  this week takes a `timezone` (IANA, such as Asia/Dubai); without one
  it is UTC, and the answer says which day it took.
- **A gap is a working day that has happened.** Days after `as_of`
  (today) are not gaps; `daily_hours` sets what a full day is (8), and
  `work_week` which days are working days: `mon_fri` (the default) or
  `sun_thu`.
- **A submitted week is locked.** Nothing is logged, changed or removed
  in it until it is reopened.
- **Hours add up.** They are kept to two decimals, summed as decimals
  and handed out as text ("1.50"), so the week's total is its days'
  totals and a budget's remainder is exact.
- **The workbook holds what was written.** Every cell is read back and
  compared before the file is returned; a meeting title that starts
  like a formula ("=…") is written as text, never run.
- **A timer is logged once.** It is marked stopped before its entry is
  made, and the entry names its timer, so a stop retried after a lost
  answer finishes the same one.
- **Sending is someone else's job.** The workbook is a file; the mail
  agent sends it.

## Sample data

Lina's week of 7 September at Sidra Office Supplies: three projects
(the Harbourline showroom, billable with a 60-hour budget; the
Riverside office move; admin), the five rules that place her meetings,
and four days logged — Monday, Tuesday and Thursday full, Wednesday
with only two hours, and Friday still to come.

## Limits

- One person's timesheet; there is no approver here, and rates and
  invoicing are out of scope.
- Weeks are ISO weeks, Monday to Sunday, so a Sunday-to-Thursday
  working week's Sunday is the last day of the ISO week before it.
- A timer is logged on the day it started; a timer that runs past
  midnight is not split across days.
- Meetings are taken as listed; the agent does not read calendars
  itself.

agent.instructions: Use this agent when the user wants to see, add, change, move or finish tasks in their Todoist. Projects, sections and labels are Todoist's own: pass a name the user said or an id a list returned, and when a function refuses a name it lists the real ones; ask the user which they meant, never invent an id, a project, a section or a label. With several Todoist accounts connected, pass account (the account's address) to every function. Priorities are the app's words: P1 is the most urgent, P4 the default. Dates: due_string takes Todoist's own words ("tomorrow", "every Monday"), due_date takes YYYY-MM-DD. For "today", "overdue", "this week" or anything Todoist's filter language says, use tasks_list with query (e.g. "today | overdue", "#Office Move & @calls", "p1"); Todoist reads "today" in the account's own time zone. A recurring task's row has next_due_date, its next occurrence. Moves each watch forward; more says a later check continues; problems lists watches that could not be read (they keep their place); closed lists watches whose project is gone.
